definition_zh: 航空公司；航线；空中直线距离；供气软管
definition_en: a company that carries passengers and goods on regular flights, the routes it flies, a straight line between two places, or a hose that supplies air
core_image: 机尾上同一枚标志，把一座座城市连成一条空中线路
scene: 清晨的候机大厅里，屏幕上的目的地一行行向上翻动，登机口前的人拖着箱子排成弯队。The airline added two morning flights between the two cities last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 airline 是「航空公司」（第 1 个义项：经营定期航班的公司）；句意为这家航空公司去年春天在两座城市之间加开了两个早班航班。画面里是候机大厅、翻动的航班屏与排队登机的旅客。

pos.zh: 名词：航空公司；航线；直线距离；供气软管

derivatives.zh: 由 airline 加名词后缀 -er 构成（也有人把它看作 air 加 liner 的组合），义为「班机；大型客机」
由 airline 加后缀 -wide 构成，义为「覆盖整个航空公司的」，如全公司范围的罢工或规定

senses.title: A company that runs regular flights
senses.titleCN: 航空公司：经营定期航班的公司
senses.definition: a business that owns or leases aircraft and carries passengers or goods on scheduled flights
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或租用飞机、按定期航班运送旅客或货物的企业
senses.example: The airline flies to more than forty cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司飞往四十多座城市。
senses.why: An airline is literally a line in the air: a company whose business is to keep aircraft moving along fixed routes, so the route and the firm share one name.
senses.whyCN: airline 字面就是「空中的一条线」：公司的生意正是让飞机沿着固定路线往返，于是「线」和「经营这条线的公司」共用一个词。

senses.title: A route flown by aircraft
senses.titleCN: 航线：飞机定期往返的空中路线
senses.definition: a route, or a set of routes, over which aircraft travel regularly between places
senses.definitionCN: 飞机定期往返于两地之间的空中路线，或这类路线的集合
senses.example: The new airline across the mountains cuts the journey to an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这条翻越群山的新航线把行程缩短到一小时。
senses.why: Before it named a company, the word named the path itself, a line drawn in the air between two points, and this old sense still lives in the route meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在指公司之前，这个词先指路线本身，即空中连接两点的线；这层古老意思仍保留在「航线」义里。

senses.title: A straight line between two points
senses.titleCN: 空中直线：两点之间的直线距离
senses.definition: a straight line between two places, especially as a measure of distance on a map
senses.definitionCN: 两地之间的直线，尤指在地图上量出的直线距离
senses.example: The airline distance between the two ports is under thirty miles.
senses.exampleCN: 两港之间的直线距离不到三十英里。
senses.why: A line in the air ignores roads and hills, so airline came to mean the shortest straight path, the distance measured as the crow flies.
senses.whyCN: 空中的线绕开道路与山丘，于是 airline 转而表示最短的直线路径，也就是「直线距离」。

senses.title: A hose that carries air
senses.titleCN: 供气软管：输送压缩空气的管子
senses.definition: a flexible tube that supplies air, as to a diver or to a pneumatic tool
senses.definitionCN: 向潜水员或气动工具等输送空气的软管
senses.example: The diver checked the airline before entering the water.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员下水前检查了供气管。
senses.why: Here the line is a physical tube rather than a route, and the air inside it is the thing being carried; the same compound simply names a line for air.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 line 是实体的管子而非路线，里面输送的东西正是 air；同一个复合词只是把「线」落实为「管」。

intro.en: Airline is a modern English compound of air, a Greek word that reached English through Latin and French, and line, a Latin word for a linen thread.
intro.cn: airline 是现代英语复合词，由 air 与 line 构成：air 是希腊词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语；line 源自拉丁语，本指亚麻线。

items.en: Greek aer named the lower, misty air; Latin borrowed it as aer, and it kept the sense of the open sky.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指下层带雾的空气；拉丁语借作 aer，保留了「开阔天空」的意思。

items.en: Old French air carried the word into English, where air means both the gas we breathe and the open space above the ground.
items.cn: 古法语 air 把这个词带入英语，air 既指我们呼吸的气体，也指地面之上的空间。

items.en: Linea meant a linen thread and, by extension, any line; it came from linum, the word for flax.
items.cn: linea 本指亚麻线，引申为任何线条；它来自表示亚麻的 linum。

items.en: The compound air line is recorded in the early nineteenth century for a straight line or direct route; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合形式 air line 在十九世纪初有记录，指直线或直飞路线；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: With powered flight the word shifted to aviation: first an air route, then a company flying it. The hose sense belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 随着动力飞行出现，这个词转向航空：先指航线，再指经营航线的公司；软管义属于二十世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the two halves of the compound and the words built on them; the near-meaning group holds the words for carriers, journeys and routes in the same field.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两半以及由它们构成的词；近义组收同一领域里表示承运者、航班与路线的词。

entries.definition: A large passenger aircraft flown by an airline; formed from airline with the suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「班机、大型客机」，指航空公司营运的客机，由 airline 加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A route for aircraft, or a passage for air; built from air plus way, the same first half as airline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航路」或「气道」，由 air 加 way 构成，前半与 airline 相同。

entries.definition: The mixture of gases we breathe and the open sky; the first element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空气、天空」，是这个复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: A long thin mark or a row of things; the second element, from Latin linea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「线、行列」，是这个词的后半部分，源自拉丁语 linea。

entries.definition: The price of a plane ticket; another compound that uses air for aviation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机票钱」，是另一个用 air 表示航空的复合词。

entries.definition: A company that transports passengers or goods, used in official and industry language for an airline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承运人、运输公司」，在官方与行业用语中可指航空公司。

entries.definition: A single journey by air; the airline is the company, the flight is the trip it sells.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航班、飞行」，airline 是公司，flight 是公司卖出的那一趟行程。

entries.definition: A fixed path between two places; the general word behind the route sense of airline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「路线」，是 airline 表示航线时背后那个更一般的词。

entries.definition: The industry and practice of flying aircraft; broader than one company or one route.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空、航空业」，比一家公司或一条航线更宽泛。

entries.definition: A service that travels back and forth between two places at short intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穿梭班机、短途往返班车」，指在两地之间频繁往返的服务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound, its recorded history and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词真实的两半、有记录的词源，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Air is the medium and line is the path: an airline is a line drawn through the sky.
normal.cn: air 是介质，line 是路径：airline 就是画在天空里的一条线。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the route, not the company; the firm is named after the line it flies.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是航线而不是公司；公司是照着它飞的那条线命名的。

normal.en: Airliner adds -er to name the aircraft, so airline is the firm and airliner is the plane.
normal.cn: airliner 加 -er 指飞机，所以 airline 是公司，airliner 是客机。

normal.en: Airfare, airway and airmail all use air in the same aviation sense.
normal.cn: airfare、airway、airmail 里的 air 都取同一个航空义。

normal.en: In airline distance the word means a straight line, the path a bird would take.
normal.cn: 在 airline distance 里，这个词指直线，也就是鸟飞的那条路。

abstract.en: Picture a map with two dots and one thin line between them; then picture a plane flying exactly along that line.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上两个点之间的一条细线，再想象一架飞机正沿着这条线飞。

abstract.en: The line can thicken into a company: offices, crews, timetables, all gathered around that one path.
abstract.cn: 这条线可以变粗成为一家公司：办公室、机组、时刻表都围着这条路径聚拢。

abstract.en: The same word can be a tube on a diver's back, because it too is a line that carries air.
abstract.cn: 同一个词也可以是潜水员背上的管子，因为它同样是一条输送空气的线。

examples.en: The airline cancelled the evening flight because of the storm.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司因暴风雨取消了晚间航班。

examples.en: Budget airlines have made short trips much cheaper.
examples.cn: 廉价航空公司让短途出行便宜了很多。

examples.en: He has worked as an airline pilot for twelve years.
examples.cn: 他做民航飞行员已经十二年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔莱恩」——爱尔在天上，莱恩是一条线：把城市连成一条空中线路的公司。

root: air 来自希腊语 aer「下层空气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；line 来自拉丁语 linea「亚麻线」，由 linum「亚麻」派生。十九世纪英语把两者合成 air line，先指空中的直线与直飞路径，二十世纪民航兴起后，又指经营定期航班的公司。

sensesIntro.en: One image runs through all four senses: a line drawn through the air, which can be a company flying it, the route itself, a straight distance, or a tube carrying air.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用一幅画面：一条画在空中的线，它可以属于经营航线的公司，可以是航线本身、直线距离，也可以是输送空气的管子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line is drawn across a map from one city to another, and an aircraft follows it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上从一座城市到另一座城市画出一条细线，一架飞机正沿着它飞行。

branches.en: THE FIRM: the line becomes a business with aircraft, crews and timetables.
branches.cn: 公司线：这条线变成一门生意，有了飞机、机组与时刻表。

branches.en: THE PATH: the route itself, flown regularly between two places.
branches.cn: 路径线：路线本身，在两地之间定期飞行。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the same line taken as the shortest distance on a map.
branches.cn: 测量线：同一条线被当作地图上的最短距离。

branches.en: THE TUBE: the line turns solid and carries air to a diver or a tool.
branches.cn: 管子线：这条线变成实体，把空气送到潜水员或工具那里。

branches.en: THE NAME: the company is named after the route it flies, which is why one word covers both.
branches.cn: 命名线：公司照着它所飞的航线取名，所以一个词同时覆盖两者。

intro.en: Airline is a compound whose two halves are old words; English then adds ordinary suffixes and combining forms to extend the family.
intro.cn: airline 是一个由两个古老词构成的复合词；英语再用普通后缀与组合形式扩展出这一族词。

latinIntro.en: Only the line half has Latin ancestors: linea and linum are recorded; aer came into Latin from Greek and is listed with that note.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 line 这一半有拉丁语祖先：linea 与 linum 均有记录；aer 是从希腊语进入拉丁语的，列入时已加说明。

items.example: It supplies the first half of airline.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 airline 的前半部分。

items.example: Latin aer is the ancestor of English air.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 aer 是英语 air 的祖先。

items.meaning: a cord, a row, a route
items.example: It supplies the second half of airline.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 airline 的后半部分。

items.example: Linea is the source of English line.
items.exampleCN: linea 是英语 line 的来源。

items.example: Linum is the plant behind linea.
items.exampleCN: linum 是 linea 背后的那种植物。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.example: It forms airliner from airline.
items.exampleCN: 它由 airline 构成 airliner。

items.example: It forms airline-wide.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 airline-wide。

items.example: It appears in airfare and airway.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 airfare 与 airway 里。

derivatives.zh: 由 airline 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「班机；大型客机」
由 airline 加后缀 -wide 构成，义为「覆盖整个航空公司的」

definition_zh: 机场；航空港；小型起降场；航站楼建筑群
definition_en: a place where aircraft take off and land, together with the buildings and services that handle passengers and cargo
core_image: 候机楼的玻璃墙外，跑道尽头的白色中线一直伸向天际
scene: 候机楼的落地玻璃外，一辆摆渡车驶过，跑道尽头的白色中线一直伸向天际。A shuttle bus took us from the terminal to the remote stand at the airport.
sceneCN: 这里 airport 是「机场」（第 1 个义项：飞机起降并集散旅客的整个场所）；句意为摆渡车把我们从航站楼送到机场的远机位。画面里是玻璃幕墙、摆渡车与跑道中线。

pos.zh: 名词：机场；航空港；小型起降场；航站楼建筑群

derivatives.zh: 由 airport 加后缀 -wide 构成，义为「覆盖整个机场的」，如全机场范围的延误或停电
由 airport 加后缀 -like 构成，义为「像机场一样的」，形容空间大、指示牌多、人流密集

senses.title: The whole place where aircraft come and go
senses.titleCN: 机场：飞机起降的整个场所
senses.definition: the entire area with runways and buildings where aircraft take off, land and are serviced
senses.definitionCN: 包含跑道与建筑、供飞机起降并进行地面保障的整片区域
senses.example: The airport was closed for two hours after the snowstorm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雪之后，机场关闭了两个小时。
senses.why: Air replaces water and port replaces harbour, so an airport is a harbour for aircraft, the whole place where they arrive and depart.
senses.whyCN: air 换掉水，port 换掉港湾，于是 airport 就是飞机的港口，即它们抵达与离开的整个场所。

senses.title: An international gateway with customs
senses.titleCN: 航空港：设海关边检的国际枢纽
senses.definition: a large airport that handles international traffic, with customs, immigration and freight facilities
senses.definitionCN: 处理国际客货流量的大型机场，设有海关、边检与货运设施
senses.example: The city hopes to turn the old airfield into an international airport.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市希望把旧机场改建成国际航空港。
senses.why: A harbour has always been a place where goods and people are inspected before entering a country, and the air version of that gateway is the international airport.
senses.whyCN: 港口从来就是货物与人员入境前接受查验的地方，这个门户搬到空中，就是国际航空港。

senses.title: A small field for light aircraft
senses.definition: a modest field with a short runway and few buildings, used by light or private aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 跑道较短、建筑简陋，供轻型或私人飞机使用的场地
senses.example: A grass airport serves the farmers during the spraying season.
senses.exampleCN: 喷洒季节里，一座草地机场为农民服务。
senses.why: The compound does not require size: any place that receives aircraft can take the name, so even a strip of grass becomes an airport.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词并不要求规模：凡能接收飞机的地方都能叫这个名字，所以一片草地也能成为 airport。

senses.title: The terminal buildings and their services
senses.titleCN: 航站楼建筑群：旅客使用的建筑与服务区
senses.definition: the buildings where passengers check in, wait, shop and board, as distinct from the runways
senses.definitionCN: 旅客办理手续、候机、购物与登机的建筑群，与跑道相对而言
senses.example: The airport is being rebuilt with a glass roof and more shops.
senses.exampleCN: 机场正在改建，将装上玻璃屋顶并增加商铺。
senses.why: Passengers meet the airport mainly indoors, so the halls and shops themselves are often meant, even though the runways are technically part of it.
senses.whyCN: 旅客主要在室内接触机场，于是大厅与商铺本身常被直接称作 airport，尽管跑道在严格意义上也属于机场。

intro.en: Airport is a modern compound of air, a Greek word that came through Latin and French, and port, a Latin word for a harbour.
intro.cn: airport 是现代复合词，由 air 与 port 构成：air 是经拉丁语与法语传来的希腊词，port 是拉丁语中表示港湾的词。

items.en: Portus meant a harbour or haven, the sheltered water where ships stopped; it is the source of English port in the harbour sense.
items.cn: portus 指港湾、避风处，即船只停靠的受保护水域；英语中表示港湾的 port 就来自它。

items.en: English borrowed port from Latin through Old French and Old English, naming a town or harbour where ships load and unload.
items.cn: 英语经古法语与古英语从拉丁语借入 port，指船只装卸货物的港城或港口。

items.en: Greek aer, the lower misty air, passed through Latin aer and Old French air; English air covers both the gas and the open sky.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指下层带雾的空气，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；英语 air 兼指气体与天空。

items.en: Airport appears in the early twentieth century for a place where aircraft land; a few dictionaries record an earlier use for airships, and the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: airport 在二十世纪初出现，指飞机降落的场所；少数词典还记录过更早指飞艇停靠处的用法，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word widens from the field itself to the international gateway and, in everyday speech, to the terminal buildings.
items.cn: 这个词从场地本身扩展到国际门户，并在日常口语里直接指航站楼建筑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compounds built with air or port; the near-meaning group gathers the landing places and buildings that sit close to airport in meaning.
note.cn: 形近组收其他由 air 或 port 构成的复合词；近义组收意义与 airport 相近的起降场地与建筑。

entries.definition: An area of ground with runways where aircraft take off and land, usually with fewer buildings than a large airport.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞机场、飞行场」，指设有跑道的起降场地，建筑通常比大型机场少；与 airport 共用 air 这一成分。

entries.definition: The part of an airport beyond security, where aircraft and passengers meet; built from air plus side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机场隔离区、空侧」，指安检之后飞机与旅客交接的区域，由 air 加 side 构成。

entries.definition: A military airfield used by an air force; another air compound for a place of landing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空军基地」，是另一个用 air 表示起降场地的复合词。

entries.definition: A port for ships; the model after which airport was formed, with sea in place of air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海港」，正是 airport 构词时仿照的对象，只是把 sea 换成 air。

entries.definition: A harbour where ships load and unload; the second half of airport, from Latin portus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「港口」，是 airport 的后半部分，来自拉丁语 portus。

entries.definition: A British term for a small airport or airfield; formed from Greek roots rather than from air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式用语，义为「小型机场、飞机场」，由希腊词根构成，而不是由 air 构成。

entries.definition: A narrow strip of ground cleared for landing and take-off, with almost no buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简易跑道、简易机场」，指平整出来供起降的狭长地带，几乎没有建筑。

entries.definition: The building where passengers check in and wait; close to the building sense of airport.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航站楼」，指旅客办手续与候机的建筑，与 airport 的建筑义最接近。

entries.definition: A central airport from which many routes radiate, used for connecting flights.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「枢纽机场」，指多条航线由此辐射、供旅客转机的中心机场。

entries.definition: A place with a landing area for helicopters; it borrows the port half but serves rotorcraft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直升机场」，指供直升机起降的场地；它借用了 port 这一半，服务对象却是旋翼机。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound, the seaport model behind it, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词真实的两半、它背后的海港构词模型，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Air plus port: a harbour for aircraft instead of ships, with runways in place of water.
normal.cn: air 加 port：把港口从船换成飞机，把水面换成跑道。

normal.en: Seaport is the model: change sea to air and the same word pattern gives airport.
normal.cn: seaport 就是模板：把 sea 换成 air，同一个构词模式就得到 airport。

normal.en: Airfield, airside and airbase show that air compounds name places and parts of places.
normal.cn: airfield、airside、airbase 说明 air 复合词可以指场地，也可以指场地的某个区域。

normal.en: At the airport is the everyday frame; airport terminal names the building you actually sit in.
normal.cn: at the airport 是日常句式；airport terminal 才是你真正坐着的建筑。

normal.en: Keep the p in port: airport is not airpot, because the second half is a harbour.
normal.cn: 留住 port 里的 p：airport 不是 airpot，因为后半部分是港口。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour with no water: ships become planes, docks become gates, and the lighthouse becomes a control tower.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有水的港口：船换成飞机，码头换成登机口，灯塔换成塔台。

abstract.en: The same harbour can be a whole field of runways, or just the glass hall where you wait.
abstract.cn: 同一座港口可以是整片跑道，也可以只是你等候的那座玻璃大厅。

abstract.en: A grass strip with one shed is still an airport, because the name belongs to the act of landing, not to the size.
abstract.cn: 一片草地加一间棚屋仍然算 airport，因为这个名字属于「起降」这件事，而不属于规模。

examples.en: We arrived at the airport two hours before the flight.
examples.cn: 我们在起飞前两小时到了机场。

examples.en: The new airport will open next summer.
examples.cn: 新机场将于明年夏天启用。

examples.en: Small airports often close in heavy fog.
examples.cn: 小型机场常在大雾中关闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔坡特」——爱尔的天空加一个港口：飞机停靠的天空港口。

root: air 来自希腊语 aer「下层空气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；port 来自拉丁语 portus「港湾」，经古法语进入英语。英语仿照 seaport 的模式把两者合成 airport，二十世纪初指飞机起降的场所，后来扩展指国际门户与航站建筑。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses keep the harbour image: a place aircraft enter and leave, which can be the whole field, the international gateway, a small strip, or the buildings passengers use.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都保留「港口」的意象：飞机进出的地方，可以是整片场地、国际门户、简易跑道，也可以是旅客使用的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a harbour is moved from the sea into the sky, with runways where the water used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：把港口从海上搬到天空，原本是水面的地方换成了跑道。

branches.en: THE WHOLE PLACE: air takes the place of water, and the port becomes a field for aircraft.
branches.cn: 整体场所线：air 取代水，港口变成供飞机使用的场地。

branches.en: THE GATEWAY: customs and immigration turn a field into a border crossing for a country.
branches.cn: 门户线：海关与边检把一片场地变成国家的出入境口岸。

branches.en: THE FIELD: size is not required, so a short grass strip still belongs to the same name.
branches.cn: 场地线：规模并非必要条件，短短一条草地跑道也叫这个名字。

branches.en: THE BUILDINGS: passengers meet the place indoors, so the halls and shops are called the airport too.
branches.cn: 建筑线：旅客在室内接触这个地方，于是大厅与商铺也被称作 airport。

branches.en: THE NODE: a large airport becomes a point where routes meet and passengers change planes.
branches.cn: 节点线：大型机场成为航线交汇、旅客换机的地点。

intro.en: Airport is a compound of two old elements; English then adds the ordinary suffixes -wide and -like to extend it.
intro.cn: airport 由两个古老成分复合而成；英语再用普通后缀 -wide 与 -like 加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Both halves have Latin records: portus for the harbour and aer for the air; porta, the Latin word for a gate, belongs to a different word and is noted here to prevent confusion.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都有拉丁语记录：portus 是港湾，aer 是空气；拉丁语 porta 是「门」，属于另一个词，此处列入以免混淆。

items.example: It supplies the first half of airport.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 airport 的前半部分。

items.example: Latin aer is the ancestor of English air.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 aer 是英语 air 的祖先。

items.example: It supplies the second half of airport.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 airport 的后半部分。

items.example: Portus is the source of port in airport.
items.exampleCN: portus 是 airport 中 port 的来源。

items.example: Porta is a different Latin word, not the source of this port.
items.exampleCN: porta 是另一个拉丁词，并非此处 port 的来源。

items.example: It forms airside.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 airside。

items.example: It forms airport-wide.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 airport-wide。

items.example: It forms airport-like.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 airport-like。

derivatives.zh: 由 airport 加后缀 -wide 构成，义为「覆盖整个机场的」
由 airport 加后缀 -like 构成，义为「像机场一样的」

definition_zh: 警报；警报器；闹钟；惊恐；使惊恐；使担忧
definition_en: a warning of danger, the device that gives it, a clock that wakes you, the fear such a warning causes, or to make someone frightened or worried
core_image: 深夜走廊里突然亮起的红色闪灯，和随之炸开的一串急促铃音
scene: 凌晨的旅馆走廊忽然响起一串急促的铃音，房门一扇扇打开，人们披着外套探出头来。The fire alarm sent everyone down the stairs in less than a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 alarm 是「警报器」（第 2 个义项：发出警报的装置）；句意为火灾警报器让所有人不到一分钟就下了楼。画面里是走廊、闪灯与披着外套的住客。

pos.zh: 名词：警报；警报器；闹钟；惊恐
动词：使惊恐；使担忧；向……报警

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「危言耸听的人」，指总把危险说得比实际更严重的人
由 alarmist 去掉 -ist 加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「危言耸听、制造恐慌的做法」
由现在分词 alarming 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「惊人地、令人担忧地」

senses.title: A warning that danger is near
senses.definition: a warning sound, signal or announcement telling people that danger or trouble is coming
senses.definitionCN: 告诉人们危险或麻烦即将到来的警示声、信号或通告
senses.example: A guard raised the alarm when he saw smoke above the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫看到屋顶上冒烟，发出了警报。
senses.why: The word began as a shout telling soldiers to seize their weapons, so its oldest job is to warn people in time to act.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是叫士兵拿起武器的喊声，所以它最古老的功能就是在还来得及行动时向人示警。

senses.title: A device that warns or wakes
senses.titleCN: 警报器：发出警报的装置
senses.definition: a machine that rings, beeps or flashes to warn of fire, smoke, intruders or another danger
senses.definitionCN: 遇火警、烟雾、入侵等危险时鸣响、鸣叫或闪光的装置
senses.example: The smoke alarm beeped twice before it began to wail.
senses.exampleCN: 烟雾警报器响了两声，随后开始尖鸣。
senses.why: Once the warning became a manufactured thing, the same noun could name the box on the ceiling rather than the cry it replaces.
senses.whyCN: 当「示警」变成一件制造出来的东西，同一个名词就能指天花板上那个盒子，而不只是它所替代的喊声。

senses.title: A clock that wakes you
senses.definition: a clock that can be set to make a noise at a chosen time in order to wake someone
senses.definitionCN: 可设定在指定时间发出声响、把人叫醒的钟
senses.example: She set her alarm for six and went to bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她把闹钟定在六点，然后上床睡了。
senses.why: Waking a sleeper is a personal, peaceful version of the battlefield shout: the alarm does the shouting so that you do not oversleep.
senses.whyCN: 叫醒熟睡的人是战场喊声的私人温和版：由闹钟替你喊，免得你睡过头。

senses.title: Sudden fear
senses.definition: a sudden feeling of fear and anxiety caused by something unexpected or threatening
senses.definitionCN: 由意外或带威胁的事物引起的突发恐惧与不安
senses.example: He jumped out of bed in alarm when the door slammed.
senses.exampleCN: 门砰地一响，他惊得从床上跳了起来。
senses.why: A call to arms is meant to startle, and the inner startle it produces became a sense of its own: the fear that arrives with the warning.
senses.whyCN: 号召拿起武器的喊声本就是为了让人一惊，而它在人心里造成的这一惊，独立成了一个义项：随警报一起到来的恐惧。

senses.title: To frighten suddenly
senses.definition: to make a person or animal suddenly afraid, especially by an unexpected sight or sound
senses.definitionCN: 尤指因意外的景象或声响使人或动物突然害怕
senses.example: The sudden noise alarmed the horses in the stable.
senses.exampleCN: 突如其来的响声惊了马厩里的马。
senses.why: The verb turns the warning into an act: something happens, the body starts, and the cause of that start is said to alarm.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「警报」变成动作：某件事发生了，身体猛地一惊，造成这一惊的东西就被说成 alarm。

senses.title: To make someone worried
senses.titleCN: 使担忧：引起警觉与不安
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel anxious and aware that something bad may be happening
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到不安，并意识到可能正发生不好的事
senses.example: Doctors are alarmed by the rise in cases among young children.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿病例的增加让医生们感到担忧。
senses.why: The fear sense slows down here: no single noise startles anyone, but a trend keeps the inner warning light on, and that steady worry is also alarm.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧义在这里放慢了：没有哪一声响把人惊起，但一种趋势让心里的警灯一直亮着，这种持续的不安同样是 alarm。

intro.en: Alarm began as a shout on the battlefield in Italy and ended up as a small clock beside a bed.
intro.cn: alarm 最初是意大利战场上的一声呐喊，最后变成了床边的一只小钟。

items.en: Arma was the plural noun for weapons and the equipment of war; the singular form is rare in classical use.
items.cn: arma 是表示武器与战具的复数名词，单数形式在古典用法中少见。

items.en: Italian all'arme, contracted from alle arme, meant 'to arms!' and was shouted to make soldiers seize their weapons.
items.cn: 意大利语 all'arme 由 alle arme 缩合而来，意为「拿起武器！」，用来喊士兵取兵器。

items.en: Old French borrowed the shout as alarme, an urgent summons to arms, and handed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语把这声呐喊借作 alarme，意为紧急征召拿起武器，并把它传给了英语。

items.en: English alarm first named a call to arms and the state of being alerted; the fear sense grew out of the startle such a call produced. First dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 alarm 最初指拿起武器的号召与受警的状态；恐惧义从这种号召引起的惊吓中长出。确切年代不确定。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun also named a bell or other device rung to warn people; the alarm clock is generally dated to the same century, and the verb to frighten grew alongside.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个名词也指用来示警的钟或其他装置；闹钟一般认为也出现在十七世纪，表示「使惊恐」的动词同期发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the word and its true family; the near-meaning group gathers warnings, loud devices and kinds of fear.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的屈折形式与真实词族；近义组收各类警告、发声装置与恐惧。

entries.definition: Frightening or worrying; the present participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人惊恐的、令人担忧的」，是现在分词作形容词用。

entries.definition: Frightened or worried by something; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受惊的、担忧的」，是过去分词作形容词用。

entries.definition: A person who spreads unnecessary fear by making dangers sound worse than they are.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「危言耸听者」，指把危险说得比实际更严重、制造不必要恐慌的人。

entries.definition: The habit of raising fear beyond what the facts support.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「危言耸听」，指超出事实依据地制造恐慌的做法。

entries.definition: An archaic spelling of alarm, kept in older poetry and stage directions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，是 alarm 的古旧拼写，仍见于较早的诗歌与舞台说明。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that tells someone about possible danger; the general word behind sense one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警告、警示」，是第一个义项背后那个更一般的词。

entries.definition: A device that makes a long wailing sound, used on police cars, ambulances or in air raids.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警笛、警报器」，指发出长鸣的装置，用于警车、救护车或空袭。

entries.definition: A sudden, overwhelming fear that spreads through a group and destroys clear thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐慌」，指在人群中蔓延、使人失去清醒判断的强烈突发恐惧。

entries.definition: A warning to be ready for danger, or the state of being watchful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「警报、警觉的」，指要求做好防备的警告或保持警惕的状态。

entries.definition: A sudden shock of fear, often shorter and more physical than alarm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「惊吓」，指突发的恐惧，通常比 alarm 更短促、更偏身体反应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Italian shout behind the word, the Latin root for weapons, and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后真实的意大利语呐喊、表示武器的拉丁词根，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: All'arme is Italian for 'to arms': the word started as a shout, not as a bell.
normal.cn: all'arme 是意大利语的「拿起武器」：这个词起初是喊声，不是铃声。

normal.en: The Latin root arma also gives army, armament and armour, all of them about weapons.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 arma 还给出 army、armament、armour，都与武器有关。

normal.en: An alarm clock puts the battlefield shout beside the bed, where it only has to wake one person.
normal.cn: 闹钟把这声战场呐喊放到床边，在那里它只需要叫醒一个人。

normal.en: A false alarm keeps the form of the warning but removes the danger.
normal.cn: false alarm 保留了警报的形式，却抽掉了危险本身。

normal.en: The verb runs at two speeds: alarmed by a noise in a second, alarmed by a trend over months.
normal.cn: 动词有两种速度：被一声响在一秒内惊到，或因一种趋势在几个月里持续担忧。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a bell rope in a dark corridor, and the sound running ahead of the danger.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在昏暗走廊里拉响铃绳，声音跑在危险前面。

abstract.en: That one rope can become a shout, a bell, a flashing lamp or a phone buzzing on a table.
abstract.cn: 同一根绳子可以变成喊声、铃、闪灯，或桌上震动的手机。

abstract.en: Fear is the echo of the shout inside the body, and it can outlast the sound by years.
abstract.cn: 恐惧是那声呐喊在身体里的回声，有时会比声音本身多活许多年。

examples.en: The alarm woke us at half past five.
examples.cn: 闹钟在五点半把我们叫醒。

examples.en: Someone pulled the fire alarm during the exam.
examples.cn: 考试期间有人拉响了火警警报器。

examples.en: The rising river alarmed the villagers.
examples.cn: 上涨的河水让村民们惊慌起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿拉姆」——阿拉一声喊，众人拿起武器：警报、惊慌、闹钟。

root: alarm 来自意大利语 all'arme「拿起武器」，是 a le arme 的缩合，其中 arme 又源自拉丁语 arma「武器」。这句战场呐喊经古法语 alarme 进入英语，先指紧急征召，再由「受警」引出警报、警报器、闹钟与惊恐诸义。

sensesIntro.en: All six senses come from one shout: it warns of danger, becomes a device that gives the warning, shrinks to a bedside clock, and leaves fear in the body that hears it.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都出自同一句呐喊：它警示危险，变成发出警示的装置，缩小成床边的闹钟，并在听见它的人身上留下恐惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shout of 'to arms' runs through a camp, and everyone starts moving at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声「拿起武器」的呐喊穿过营地，所有人同时动了起来。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: the shout turns into any warning that danger is near.
branches.cn: 信号线：呐喊转化为任何提示危险临近的警告。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: the warning is built into machines, from a smoke detector to a clock beside the bed.
branches.cn: 装置线：警告被做进机器，从烟雾探测器到床边的钟。

branches.en: THE EMOTION: the startle of the shout becomes a sudden fear with a name of its own.
branches.cn: 情绪线：呐喊带来的那一惊，变成有独立名称的突发恐惧。

branches.en: THE SUDDEN ACT: to alarm is to cause that startle in a person or an animal.
branches.cn: 突发动作线：alarm 作动词，就是使人或动物产生那一惊。

branches.en: THE SLOW ACT: to alarm can also mean to keep someone quietly worried about a trend.
branches.cn: 缓慢动作线：作动词也可以指让人对某种趋势持续地隐隐不安。

intro.en: Alarm is a borrowing from Italian through French; English then adds ordinary suffixes to build its family.
intro.cn: alarm 是经法语来自意大利语的借词；英语随后用普通后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun arma and the verb armare are both recorded; the Italian shout and the French noun are documented forms between them and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 arma 与动词 armare 均有记录；意大利语呐喊与法语名词都是有文献的形式，位于拉丁语与英语之间。

items.example: It contracts a and le before a vowel.
items.exampleCN: 它在元音前把 a 与 le 缩合。

items.example: Arme is the noun inside the shout all'arme.
items.exampleCN: arme 是呐喊 all'arme 里的那个名词。

items.example: Latin arma is the root of the Italian noun.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 arma 是意大利语名词的词根。

items.meaning: a call to arms, an urgent summons
items.meaningCN: 拿起武器的号召；紧急征召
items.example: Old French alarme carried the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 alarme 把这个词带进了英语。

items.example: It forms alarming.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alarming。

items.example: It forms alarmed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alarmed。

items.meaning: a person who does or favours something
items.meaningCN: 做某事或主张某事的人
items.example: It forms alarmist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alarmist。

items.example: It forms alarmism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alarmism。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「危言耸听的人」
由本词加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「危言耸听、制造恐慌的做法」
由现在分词 alarming 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「惊人地、令人担忧地」

definition_zh: 音乐专辑；相册；集邮册；签名纪念册；（古罗马）白色公告板
definition_en: a collection of recorded songs issued together, a book for keeping photographs, stamps or signatures, or the whitened board on which public notices were written in ancient Rome
core_image: 一本硬壳大书摊在膝上，纸页里贴着一排排小方片
scene: 客厅的矮柜里躺着一本硬壳大书，翻开是婚礼那天的照片，边角已经微微发黄。She opened the album and found a photograph of her grandmother at twenty.
sceneCN: 这里 album 是「相册」（第 2 个义项：收集照片的册子）；句意为她翻开相册，找到一张祖母二十岁时的照片。画面里是矮柜、硬壳书与泛黄的照片。

pos.zh: 名词：音乐专辑；相册；集邮册；签名纪念册；古罗马公告板

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 mini- 与 album 组合而成，义为「迷你专辑」，指曲目较少、时长较短的发行形式
由 album 与 -oriented 组合而成，义为「以专辑为导向的」，多用于描述电台的编排格式

senses.title: A collection of recorded songs
senses.titleCN: 音乐专辑：成套发行的录音作品
senses.definition: a set of recorded songs or pieces released together as one work, on disc, tape or in digital form
senses.definitionCN: 作为一件作品成套发行的录音歌曲或乐曲，载体可以是唱片、磁带或数字文件
senses.example: Their second album sold a million copies in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的第二张专辑一个月内卖出一百万张。
senses.why: Early records were sold in a book-like sleeve holding several discs, so the container's name moved onto the collection of songs inside it.
senses.whyCN: 早期的唱片装在一个像书一样、能装几张唱片的封套里，于是容器的名字转移到了里面那一组歌曲上。

senses.title: A book of photographs
senses.definition: a book with blank pages or pockets in which photographs are kept
senses.definitionCN: 有空白页或插袋、用来存放照片的册子
senses.example: The wedding album sat on the shelf for years without being opened.
senses.exampleCN: 那本婚礼相册在书架上放了好几年都没被翻开。
senses.why: Album first meant a blank surface for writing, and photographs are simply what people began pasting onto that blank surface.
senses.whyCN: album 最初指可供书写的空白表面，而照片不过是人们后来贴到这个空白表面上的东西。

senses.title: A book for stamps and clippings
senses.titleCN: 集邮册：贴存邮票与剪报的册子
senses.definition: a book with pages for mounting stamps, postcards, newspaper cuttings or other small flat items
senses.definitionCN: 页面可固定邮票、明信片、剪报或其他小件平面收藏品的册子
senses.example: He pasted every foreign stamp into a green album.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每一枚外国邮票都贴进一本绿色集邮册。
senses.why: The same blank book serves any small flat treasure, so stamps and clippings simply repeat the collecting gesture that photographs had already taught.
senses.whyCN: 同一本空白册子可以服务任何小件平面收藏品，于是邮票与剪报只是重复照片已经教会人们的那个「收集」动作。

senses.title: A book of signatures and memories
senses.titleCN: 签名纪念册：留字留念的册子
senses.definition: a book in which friends, guests or classmates write their names, wishes or short messages as a keepsake
senses.definitionCN: 请朋友、来客或同学写下姓名、祝愿或短句以作留念的册子
senses.example: Her classmates filled an album with wishes before she moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬走之前，同学们在一本纪念册里写满了祝福。
senses.why: This is the oldest modern use: a blank book passed from hand to hand, so that the writing itself becomes the collection.
senses.whyCN: 这是这本书最早的现代用法：一本空白册子在人们手中传递，写下的字本身就成了被收藏的内容。

senses.title: The whitened notice board of Rome
senses.titleCN: 古罗马白色公告板：张贴公告的涂白木板
senses.definition: in ancient Rome, a board whitened with gypsum on which public notices, lists and announcements were written
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马用石膏涂白的木板，上面书写公告、名单与通告
senses.example: In Rome a notice of the games was painted on an album in the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 在罗马，竞技公告被写在广场的一块白色公告板上。
senses.why: The Latin word named a whitened board before it named a book, and this is the literal image from which every later collection sense grows.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词先指涂白的木板，后指册子；正是这块板子的具体形象，长出了后来所有的「收集」义。

intro.en: Album comes straight from Latin, where it began as a whitened board and ended as a blank book.
intro.cn: album 直接来自拉丁语，在那里它先是一块涂白的木板，后来才成为空白册子。

items.en: Albus was the adjective for white or pale; it is the colour word behind the whole family, including albedo and albino.
items.cn: albus 是表示「白色、苍白」的形容词，是 albedo、albino 等一整族词背后的颜色词。

items.en: The neuter noun album meant a white tablet or board, especially one whitened with gypsum for public notices and lists.
items.cn: 中性名词 album 指白色的板或牌，尤指用石膏涂白、供书写公告与名单的木板。

items.en: Medieval Latin extended album from the board to the written list itself, and then to a blank book or register kept for entries.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把 album 从木板扩展到写在上面的名单，再扩展到供人题写的空白册子或登记簿。

items.en: English album is recorded in the seventeenth century for a blank book in which friends wrote names and verses; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 album 在十七世纪有记录，指供朋友写下姓名与赠言的空白册子；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Photograph and stamp albums belong to the nineteenth century; the recorded-music album grew out of book-like record sleeves in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 照片相册与集邮册属于十九世纪；唱片专辑则从二十世纪那种像书一样的唱片封套中发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin colour root albus; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of collected works and books.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁颜色词根 albus 的一族词；近义组收其他类型的作品合集与册子。

entries.definition: The proportion of light a surface reflects; a scientific word built on Latin albus, white.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反照率、反射率」，指表面反射光的比例；由拉丁语 albus「白」构成。

entries.definition: A person or animal born with no pigment in skin, hair or eyes; formed from the same white root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「白化病患者、白化动物」，指出生时皮肤、毛发或眼睛缺少色素者；同出「白」这一词根。

entries.definition: The white of an egg; the Latin noun albumen also meant egg white, from albus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛋白、蛋清」；拉丁语 albumen 本也指蛋清，源自 albus。

entries.definition: A white linen robe worn by priests; a church word from the Latin adjective for white.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「白麻布长袍」，是神职人员穿的礼服；来自拉丁语表示白色的形容词。

entries.definition: A collection of pieces gathered from various sources into one work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合集、汇编」，指从不同来源收集作品编成一册或一张。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for pasting in photographs, cuttings and small keepsakes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剪贴簿」，指空白页可粘贴照片、剪报与小纪念品的册子。

entries.definition: A published collection of poems or stories by different writers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选集、诗文集」，指把不同作者的诗或小说编在一起出版的书。

entries.definition: A flat case, or the set of works it holds, used to show an artist's or designer's output.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「作品集、画夹」，指装作品的扁平夹子或其中展示艺术家成果的一组作品。

entries.definition: A disc carrying recorded sound; the physical object an album is played from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「唱片」，指承载录音的圆盘，即播放专辑所用的实物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root albus, the board-to-book history, and the phrases album appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 albus、从木板到册子的词义史，以及 album 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Albus means white: the first album was a board whitened with gypsum so that notices would stand out.
normal.cn: albus 意为白色：最早的 album 是一块用石膏涂白的木板，好让公告更醒目。

normal.en: The word moved from board to list to blank book, which is why a photo album and a stamp album feel like the same object.
normal.cn: 这个词从木板走到名单，再走到空白册子，所以相册与集邮册感觉是同一种东西。

normal.en: Albedo, albino and albumen all keep the white idea, though their meanings moved far from paper.
normal.cn: albedo、albino、albumen 都保留了「白」的观念，尽管词义已经远离纸张。

normal.en: A studio album is recorded in a studio; a debut album is the first one a band releases.
normal.cn: studio album 是在录音室录的专辑；debut album 是乐队发行的第一张。

normal.en: The album cover is the book cover of this modern book of songs.
normal.cn: album cover 就是这本现代「歌本」的封面。

abstract.en: Picture a white board in a Roman square, then the same white surface bound into pages.
abstract.cn: 想象罗马广场上的一块白板，再想象同一片白色被装订成页。

abstract.en: The pages can hold photographs, stamps, signatures or songs; the container stays, the contents change.
abstract.cn: 这些页面可以装照片、邮票、签名或歌曲；容器不变，内容不断更换。

abstract.en: An album is an argument that separate small things belong together.
abstract.cn: album 本身就是一个主张：一件件小东西应当被放在一起。

examples.en: Their second album sold a million copies.
examples.cn: 他们的第二张专辑卖出了一百万张。

examples.en: She keeps every holiday photo in a thick album.
examples.cn: 她把每张假日照片都收在一本厚相册里。

examples.en: The band is recording a new album in London.
examples.cn: 乐队正在伦敦录制一张新专辑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿尔本」——阿尔白白的，本子也白白的：先贴公告，再贴照片与歌。

root: album 直接借自拉丁语 album，本义是「涂白的板」，来自形容词 albus「白色」。古罗马人把公告写在涂了石膏的白板上，中世纪拉丁语再由「白板上的名单」引申为空白登记册，英语十七世纪用它指题字留念的册子，十九世纪起指相册与集邮册，二十世纪又指唱片专辑。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses are the same blank surface: a whitened board for notices, then a blank book for signatures, photographs, stamps, and finally a sleeve for songs.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都是同一片空白表面：先是贴公告的白板，再是题字、贴照片、贴邮票的空白册子，最后是装歌曲的封套。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white board waits for writing, and later the same white surface is bound into pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块白板等着被书写，后来同一片白色被装订成了书页。

branches.en: THE SONGS: a book-like sleeve holds discs, and its name passes to the songs inside.
branches.cn: 歌曲线：像书一样的封套装着唱片，名字便转到了里面的歌曲上。

branches.en: THE PHOTOGRAPHS: the blank page becomes a place to keep images.
branches.cn: 照片线：空白页面成了保存影像的地方。

branches.en: THE STAMPS: any small flat treasure can be pasted onto the same page.
branches.cn: 邮票线：任何小件平面收藏品都能贴到同样的页面上。

branches.en: THE SIGNATURES: friends write on the blank page, and the writing itself is the collection.
branches.cn: 签名线：朋友在空白页上写字，写下的字本身就是收藏。

branches.en: THE BOARD: the Roman notice board is the literal white surface behind every later sense.
branches.cn: 木板线：古罗马的公告板是后来所有义项背后那片具体的白色表面。

intro.en: Album is a Latin noun with a Latin adjective inside it; English adds combining forms and suffixes to build new words around it.
intro.cn: album 是一个内含拉丁形容词的拉丁名词；英语再用组合形式与后缀在它周围造新词。

latinIntro.en: Albus, album, albumen and albedo are all recorded Latin forms, so nothing in this family needs to be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: albus、album、albumen 与 albedo 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，这一族词无需重构。

items.example: Albus is the colour word inside album.
items.exampleCN: albus 是 album 里面的那个颜色词。

items.example: The root appears in albino and albedo.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在 albino 与 albedo 里。

items.example: The Latin noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the gender of Latin album.
items.exampleCN: 它标出拉丁语 album 的性。

items.example: It forms photo album.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 photo album。

items.example: It forms mini-album.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 mini-album。

items.example: It forms album-oriented.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 album-oriented。

items.meaningCN: 构成 albumen 这类名词的词尾
items.example: It appears in albumen.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 albumen 里。

latinEntries.meaning: a white board for notices; a register

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 mini- 与 album 组合而成，义为「迷你专辑」
由 album 与 -oriented 组合而成，义为「以专辑为导向的」

definition_zh: 乙醇；酒精；醇类；酒类；含酒精饮料；消毒酒精
definition_en: the chemical ethanol, the class of organic compounds it belongs to, drinks that contain it, or the liquid used for cleaning and as a fuel
core_image: 一只透明细颈瓶，清亮的液体几乎看不见，只在瓶壁上留下一道亮痕
scene: 厨房台面上放着一小瓶透明液体，旁边的棉球和纱布还没收好，窗外的光穿过瓶子，在桌面上留下一道亮痕。She cleaned the cut with a little alcohol before putting on a plaster.
sceneCN: 这里 alcohol 是「消毒酒精」（第 4 个义项：外用的乙醇制剂）；句意为她先用一点酒精清洁伤口，再贴上创可贴。画面里是透明瓶、棉球、纱布与桌上的亮痕。

pos.zh: 名词：乙醇；酒精；醇类；酒类；消毒酒精

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ic 构成，义为「含酒精的」；作名词指「酗酒者、酒精依赖者」
由 alcoholic 去掉 -ic 加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「酒精依赖、酗酒」
由本词加后缀 -free 构成，义为「不含酒精的」，多用于饮料标签
由本词加后缀 -ate 构成，义为「醇化物」，是化学中指醇与金属或碱结合的产物的术语

senses.title: The chemical ethanol
senses.titleCN: 乙醇：酒精这种化学物质
senses.definition: a clear flammable liquid, the intoxicating substance in drinks and a common solvent and fuel
senses.definitionCN: 一种无色易燃的液体，是酒类中的致醉成分，也常用作溶剂与燃料
senses.example: The lab stores pure alcohol in a locked cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把纯酒精锁在柜子里。
senses.why: Modern chemistry fixed the old word onto one molecule, so alcohol now names ethanol itself, whether it comes from a still or a factory.
senses.whyCN: 现代化学把这个古老的词固定在一个分子上，于是 alcohol 现在指乙醇本身，无论它来自蒸馏器还是工厂。

senses.title: The class of alcohols
senses.titleCN: 醇类：含羟基的有机化合物
senses.definition: any member of a large class of organic compounds containing a hydroxyl group, such as methanol or ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 含羟基的一大类有机化合物中的任何一种，如甲醇或乙醇
senses.example: The course compares alcohols with acids and ethers.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把醇类与酸、醚作比较。
senses.why: Once chemists saw that many liquids share the same reactive group, the name had to stretch from one substance to a whole family.
senses.whyCN: 当化学家发现许多液体共有同一个反应基团时，这个名字就必须从一种物质扩展到整个家族。

senses.title: Drinks that contain it
senses.definition: alcoholic drinks taken together, such as beer, wine and spirits
senses.definitionCN: 合起来看的含酒精饮料，如啤酒、葡萄酒与烈酒
senses.example: The hotel does not serve alcohol after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆午夜之后不再供应酒。
senses.why: People met the substance mainly in what they drank, so the name of the liquid became the name of the drinks that carry it.
senses.whyCN: 人们主要通过饮品接触这种物质，于是液体的名字变成了承载它的那些饮品的名字。

senses.title: The liquid used for cleaning
senses.titleCN: 消毒酒精：外用的乙醇制剂
senses.definition: a solution of ethanol used outside the body to clean skin, tools or surfaces, or as a solvent
senses.definitionCN: 用于体表、器具或表面清洁的乙醇溶液，也可作溶剂
senses.example: Wipe the thermometer with alcohol before you use it.
senses.exampleCN: 使用温度计之前先用酒精擦一擦。
senses.why: The same molecule that makes a drink intoxicating kills germs, so a household bottle of alcohol belongs to the cleaning shelf rather than the bar.
senses.whyCN: 让饮品致醉的同一个分子也能杀菌，所以家里那瓶酒精放在清洁架上，而不是酒柜里。

senses.title: Strong distilled spirits
senses.titleCN: 烈酒：蒸馏而成的高度酒
senses.definition: strong drink produced by distillation, such as whisky, brandy or vodka, rather than beer or wine
senses.definitionCN: 经蒸馏制成的高度酒，如威士忌、白兰地或伏特加，与啤酒、葡萄酒相对
senses.example: Vodka is a strong alcohol distilled from grain or potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 伏特加是用谷物或马铃薯蒸馏而成的高度酒。
senses.why: Distillation concentrates the spirit, and English often uses alcohol for the strong result, the drink where the substance is most obvious.
senses.whyCN: 蒸馏把酒精度提了上去，英语常用 alcohol 指蒸馏出来的高度酒，也就是那种物质最显眼的饮品。

intro.en: Alcohol travelled from an Arabic word for a dark eye powder to the name of a clear liquid, through medieval Latin and early chemistry.
intro.cn: alcohol 从一个指深色眼妆粉的阿拉伯词，经中世纪拉丁语与早期化学，走到了指一种清澈液体的名称。

items.en: Kuhl was powdered antimony, a dark mineral used as eye cosmetic; the word named the powder, not a drink.
items.cn: kuhl 指锑的粉末，是一种用作眼妆的深色矿物；这个词指粉末，不是饮品。

items.en: With the definite article al-, al-kuhl meant 'the kuhl'; the article is the al- at the front of the modern word.
items.cn: 加上定冠词 al- 后，al-kuhl 意为「那种锑粉」；这个冠词就是现代词开头的 al-。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed alcohol for antimony powder and then widened it to any fine powder or distilled essence.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入 alcohol 指锑粉，随后扩展到任何细粉或蒸馏所得的精华。

items.en: English alcohol first meant a fine powder made by sublimation; the phrase alcohol of wine for distilled spirit is recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语 alcohol 最初指升华制成的细粉；十七世纪有 alcohol of wine 的说法，指蒸馏所得的酒之精华。

items.en: Around 1800 chemistry fixed alcohol on ethanol and on the class of alcohols; the older sense of strong drink survives in everyday use.
items.cn: 约在十九世纪初，化学把 alcohol 固定在乙醇与醇类上；较早的「烈酒」义仍在日常用法中留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built from alcohol; the near-meaning group gathers the chemical name, the drinks and the informal words for them.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alcohol 构成的英语词；近义组收化学名称、酒类以及它们口语化的说法。

entries.definition: Containing alcohol, or a person dependent on it; formed with the suffix -ic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含酒精的」；作名词指「酒精依赖者」，由本词加后缀 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: The condition of being unable to control drinking; formed with the suffix -ism.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒精依赖、酗酒」，指无法控制饮酒的状况，由本词加后缀 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: A drink with no alcohol in it; the negative prefix non- is added to alcoholic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不含酒精的」，指饮品中没有酒精；是加否定前缀 non- 构成。

entries.definition: A label meaning that a product contains no alcohol at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无酒精的」，是产品标签上的说法，表示完全不含酒精。

entries.definition: An instrument for measuring how much alcohol a liquid contains; built from alcohol plus meter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒精比重计」，指测量液体酒精含量的仪器，由 alcohol 加 meter 构成。

entries.definition: The systematic chemical name for the alcohol in drinks and in fuel blends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「乙醇」，是酒类与燃料混合液中所含酒精的化学系统名称。

entries.definition: Strong alcoholic drink, especially distilled spirits; more formal than booze.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烈酒、酒」，尤指蒸馏酒，比口语词更正式。

entries.definition: Distilled drinks such as whisky or gin; the word keeps the old image of a distilled essence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烈酒」，如威士忌或杜松子酒；这个词仍保留着「蒸馏出的精华」这一古老意象。

entries.definition: An informal word for alcohol or a drinking session.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒、喝酒」，是口语说法。

entries.definition: Any liquid you swallow; in social use it can mean an alcoholic one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「饮料」，泛指任何可饮用的液体；在社交语境里也可专指含酒精的饮品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Arabic source, the article hidden at the front, and the chemistry that reshaped the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的阿拉伯语来源、藏在词首的冠词，以及重塑了词义的化学。

normal.en: Al-kuhl was antimony powder for the eyes: the word began as a mineral powder, not as a drink.
normal.cn: al-kuhl 是画眼用的锑粉：这个词起初是矿物粉末，不是饮品。

normal.en: The al- at the front is simply the Arabic word for 'the', so alcohol literally contains a definite article.
normal.cn: 开头的 al- 就是阿拉伯语的定冠词「那个」，所以 alcohol 字面上含着一个定冠词。

normal.en: Chemistry split the word in two: alcohol is ethanol, while alcohols are the whole class.
normal.cn: 化学把这个词分成两层：alcohol 指乙醇，alcohols 指整个醇类。

normal.en: Distillation is the hinge: it concentrates the spirit and gives the word its strong-drink sense.
normal.cn: 蒸馏是转轴：它把酒之精华浓缩起来，也让这个词有了「烈酒」义。

normal.en: Rubbing alcohol goes on cotton wool, not into a glass; the same word changes shelf.
normal.cn: rubbing alcohol 是倒在棉球上的，不是倒进杯里的；同一个词换了一个货架。

abstract.en: Picture a dark powder being sieved in an old pharmacy, then a clear liquid in a glass vial on a lab bench.
abstract.cn: 想象老药房里有人在筛深色粉末，再想象实验台上一只装着清亮液体的玻璃小瓶。

abstract.en: One word covers a molecule, a chemical class, a drink and a cleaner: the same substance seen from four distances.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖一个分子、一个化学类别、一种饮品和一瓶清洁剂：同一种物质在四个距离上被看见。

abstract.en: The long road from eye powder to fuel shows how a name can travel until only the substance remains.
abstract.cn: 从眼妆粉到燃料的漫长道路说明：一个名字可以一路迁徙，最后只剩下它所指的是那种物质。

examples.en: This drink contains no alcohol at all.
examples.cn: 这种饮料完全不含酒精。

examples.en: Rubbing alcohol is kept in the first-aid box.
examples.cn: 外用消毒酒精放在急救箱里。

examples.en: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol during fermentation.
examples.cn: 发酵过程中，酵母把糖变成酒精。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿尔科霍尔」——阿尔是冠词，科霍尔是锑粉：从画眼的粉末走到清亮的酒。

root: alcohol 来自阿拉伯语 al-kuhl，其中 al- 是定冠词，kuhl 指用作眼妆的锑粉。中世纪拉丁语借作 alcohol，先指锑粉，再泛指细粉与蒸馏所得的精华；英语十六世纪借入，十七世纪用它指蒸馏酒，十九世纪化学把它固定为乙醇及醇类。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move outward from one substance: ethanol itself, the whole chemical class, the drinks that carry it, the bottle used for cleaning, and the strong spirits produced by distillation.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从一种物质向外展开：乙醇本身、整个化学类别、承载它的酒类、用于清洁的那瓶液体，以及蒸馏出的烈酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine powder is distilled into a clear liquid that can clean, burn or intoxicate.
core.cn: 核心意象：细粉被蒸馏成一种清亮液体，它能清洁、能燃烧，也能使人醉。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: chemistry fixes the old word on ethanol, a clear flammable liquid.
branches.cn: 分子线：化学把这个古老的词固定在乙醇上，一种无色易燃的液体。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the name stretches from one substance to every compound with the same group.
branches.cn: 类别线：名字从一种物质扩展到所有含同一基团的化合物。

branches.en: THE DRINK: the substance is met mainly in beer, wine and spirits, so the word names them.
branches.cn: 饮品线：人们主要在啤酒、葡萄酒与烈酒中接触这种物质，于是这个词也指这些饮品。

branches.en: THE CLEANER: the same liquid kills germs, so a bottle of it sits with cotton wool and bandages.
branches.cn: 清洁线：同一种液体能杀菌，于是那瓶东西与棉球、绷带放在一起。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: distillation concentrates the drink and produces the strong spirits the word often means.
branches.cn: 烈酒线：蒸馏浓缩了饮品，造出这个词常指的烈性酒。

intro.en: Alcohol is a borrowing whose Arabic article is still visible; English and chemistry then add suffixes and prefixes to build the modern family.
intro.cn: alcohol 是一个借词，阿拉伯语冠词至今可见；英语与化学再用后缀、前缀构造现代词族。

latinIntro.en: The medieval Latin noun alcohol is recorded with the powder and distillate senses; the Arabic source is given beside it because the word is not native Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语名词 alcohol 有粉末与蒸馏物两种义项的记录；由于它不是拉丁语本族词，阿拉伯语来源一并列出。

items.exampleCN: 它位于 al-kuhl 的开头。

items.meaning: powdered antimony used as eye cosmetic
items.example: Kuhl is the noun inside the Arabic phrase.
items.exampleCN: kuhl 是这个阿拉伯语短语里的名词。

items.example: Medieval Latin alcohol carried both senses.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 alcohol 兼具这两种意思。

items.example: It appears in ethanol and methanol.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 ethanol 与 methanol 里。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 alcoholism。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 non-alcoholic。

latinEntries.meaning: powder of antimony; a distilled essence

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ic 构成，义为「含酒精的」，作名词指「酒精依赖者」
由本词加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「酒精依赖、酗酒」
由本词加后缀 -free 构成，义为「不含酒精的」
由本词加后缀 -ate 构成，义为「醇化物」，是化学术语

definition_zh: 活着的；有活力的；仍存在的；充满……的；意识到的；生动热闹的
definition_en: living and not dead, full of energy, still in existence, teeming with something, aware of something, or vivid and busy
core_image: 薄毯下一起一伏的胸口，热气还留在身体里
scene: 矿井塌方后的第三天，救援队停下钻机侧耳细听。The trapped miner was still alive behind the wall of rock.
sceneCN: 这里 alive 是「活着的」（第 1 个义项：仍有生命、尚未死亡）；句意为被困矿工在岩壁后面仍然活着。画面里可辨认的是钻机、矿灯与碎石。

pos.zh: 形容词（多作表语）：活着的；有活力的；仍存在的；充满……的；意识到的

collocations.zh: 使……延续下去；让……保持活力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「活力；生机；仍活着的事实」
由同源名词 life 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；生动的」，属同一词族而非直接派生
与本词同出古英语 lif，是这个词族的根词，义为「生命；生活」

senses.title: Living, not dead
senses.definition: having life; continuing to live rather than being dead
senses.definitionCN: 拥有生命；仍在活着，而不是已经死亡
senses.example: The doctors worked all night to keep the premature baby alive.
senses.exampleCN: 医生彻夜抢救，让早产的婴儿活了下来。
senses.why: The word began as the phrase on life, meaning in life; whatever is still in life has not left it, and that is exactly the first sense, being alive rather than dead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来只是短语 on life，意思是「在生命之中」；还在生命里的，就是还没有离开生命，这正是第一个义项：活着，而不是死了。

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.definition: full of energy, interest or excitement; lively in manner or mood
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力、兴趣或兴奋；神态或情绪上生气勃勃
senses.example: A cup of coffee made him feel alive again after the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途开车之后，一杯咖啡让他重新有了精神。
senses.why: If being on life means life is still in the body, the same picture can brighten: life shows itself as heat and movement, so a person who shows them is called alive.
senses.whyCN: 既然「在生命之中」意味着生命还在身体里，同一幅画面就可以变亮：生命以热度和动作显现，所以把这种显现带在身上的人，就被说成 alive。

senses.title: Still in existence
senses.definition: continuing to exist, operate or matter, instead of dying out or being forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 继续存在、运作或起作用，而不是消亡或被遗忘
senses.example: The old craft is still alive in a few mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这门古老的手艺在几个山村里仍在延续。
senses.why: A craft or a question can be treated like a body: as long as it is still in life, it has not died, so the word spreads from creatures to things that endure.
senses.whyCN: 手艺或问题可以被当作身体来看待：只要它还在「生命之中」，就没有死去；于是这个词从生物扩展到仍在延续的事物。

senses.title: Teeming with something
senses.definition: filled or crowded with living, moving things, used in the pattern alive with
senses.definitionCN: 满是活的、在动的东西，用于 alive with 这一句式
senses.example: At dusk the pond is alive with frogs and insects.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时池塘里到处都是青蛙和昆虫。
senses.why: A place alive with creatures holds so much life that the life seems to spill into the place itself; the container takes on the quality of what fills it.
senses.whyCN: 一个 alive with 生物的地方，装着的生命多到像是溢到地方本身上；容器于是染上了所装之物的性质，这就是「充满、到处是」的来历。

senses.title: Aware of something
senses.definition: aware of something and quick to notice or respond to it, used in the pattern alive to
senses.definitionCN: 察觉到某事并能迅速作出反应，用于 alive to 这一句式
senses.example: A good editor stays alive to changes in the language.
senses.exampleCN: 好的编辑对语言的变化始终保持敏感。
senses.why: Being alive is being awake to the world; a mind that registers a danger or a shift is as responsive as a living body, so the word takes on the sense of being alert.
senses.whyCN: 活着就是对外界保持醒觉；能察觉到危险或变化的心思，就像有反应的身体一样，于是这个词有了「警觉、意识到」的意思。

senses.title: Vivid and full of activity
senses.definition: vivid, animated or busy, especially in the phrase come alive
senses.definitionCN: 鲜明、有生气或繁忙，尤用于 come alive 这一短语
senses.example: The market comes alive at dawn, when the fishing boats return.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明渔船回港时，市场就热闹起来。
senses.why: Life as heat and motion also applies to a scene: when a silent place begins to sound and move, it is said to come alive, as if it had been dead.
senses.whyCN: 生命等于热度与动作，这个画面也用在场景上：安静的地方开始有人声和走动，就像从死寂里恢复过来，于是说它 come alive。

intro.en: Alive is not a Latin borrowing but a worn-down English phrase: the preposition on fused with the noun life.
intro.cn: alive 不是拉丁语借词，而是一个被磨短的英语短语：介词 on 与名词 life 粘成了一个词。

items.en: Lif meant life, existence, the state of being a living creature; the noun is well recorded, though its exact relation to the verb libban is a matter of detail.
items.cn: lif 意为「生命、生存、活着的状态」；这个名词有充分记录，它与动词 libban 的确切关系属于细节问题。

items.en: The phrase on life, literally on life or in life, said that someone was still living; on here had the sense of being in a state.
items.cn: 短语 on life 字面是「在生命上、在生命之中」，用来表示某人仍然活着；这里的 on 带有「处于某种状态」的意思。

items.en: In Middle English the unstressed on- merged with life into a single word, alife, and the vowel was shortened in everyday speech.
items.cn: 中古英语里，弱读的 on- 与 life 合并成一个词 alife，日常说话中元音也随之缩短。

items.en: The modern spelling alive settles in this period; the word is already mainly predicative, while living takes over the place before a noun.
items.cn: 现代拼写 alive 在这一时期定型；此时它已主要作表语，而名词前的位置由 living 接替。

items.en: The old phrase grows new branches: alive with for a place full of creatures, alive to for a mind that notices, and come alive for a scene that starts to move.
items.cn: 这个古老短语长出新枝：alive with 指地方满是生物，alive to 指心思有所察觉，come alive 指场景开始有了动静。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the lif family and adjectives that share the a- predicative pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words for being living, energetic or still in existence.
note.cn: 形近组收 lif 词族与同样采用 a- 表语模式的形容词；近义组收表示有生命、有活力与仍然存在的词。

entries.definition: The noun for existence as a living being; it is the noun inside the old phrase on life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生命、生活」，正是古老短语 on life 所依附的那个名词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun for being alive, and the form used before a noun where alive cannot stand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与名词，义为「活着的、生计」，也是可以放在名词前而 alive 不能的位置上的形式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning full of energy; it is built on life rather than directly on alive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活泼的、生动的」，由 life 加后缀构成，而不是直接从 alive 派生。

entries.definition: An adjective that also begins with a- and is used predicatively; only the pattern is alike, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「醒着的」，同样以 a- 开头且作表语；它只是拼写模式相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Full of energy and determination; a close match for the energetic sense of alive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精神饱满的、有干劲的」，与 alive 表示有活力的义项最接近。

entries.definition: Having life, used mainly in scientific writing about living things as opposed to inanimate matter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有生命的」，主要用于科学写作，与无生命的物质相对。

entries.definition: Still in existence, especially of documents, species or old buildings; formal and narrower than alive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「现存的」，多用于文献、物种或古建筑，语气正式，范围比 alive 窄。

entries.definition: Noticing or knowing something; the plain equivalent of the alive to pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意识到的、知道的」，正是 alive to 这一句式的平实说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real origin of the word, an English phrase rather than a Latin root, and the frames it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实来历，即一个英语短语而不是拉丁词根，以及它实际出现的句式。

normal.en: Alive is a phrase in disguise: on plus life, meaning in life, worn down to a single word.
normal.cn: alive 是一个伪装起来的短语：on 加 life，意思是「在生命之中」，磨短成了一个词。

normal.en: The a- at the front is the old preposition on, the same pattern as in asleep and awake.
normal.cn: 词首的 a- 就是古老的介词 on，与 asleep、awake 是同一个模式。

normal.en: Life, living and lively share the root lif, so the whole family keeps speaking of life.
normal.cn: life、living、lively 共享词根 lif，整个词族始终在说「生命」。

normal.en: Alive is predicative: we say the patient is alive, but a living patient, never an alive patient.
normal.cn: alive 作表语：可以说 the patient is alive，但要说 a living patient，绝不说 an alive patient。

normal.en: Alive with and alive to are two fixed frames: one is full of creatures, the other full of attention.
normal.cn: alive with 与 alive to 是两个固定框架：一个装满生物，一个装满注意力。

abstract.en: Picture a chest rising and falling under a thin blanket: that small movement is the whole meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象薄毯下一起一伏的胸口：那点起伏就是这个词的全部意思。

abstract.en: Then the same warmth leaves the body and fills a whole room, and the room is alive too.
abstract.cn: 接着同一股热气离开身体、充满整个房间，房间也活了起来。

abstract.en: Finally the warmth turns into attention: a mind that notices everything around it is alive in the same way.
abstract.cn: 最后这股热气变成注意力：能察觉四周一切动静的心思，也是以同样的方式活着。

examples.en: The doctors worked all night to keep the premature baby alive.
examples.cn: 医生彻夜抢救，让早产的婴儿活了下来。

examples.en: The square comes alive on summer evenings, when the musicians set up.
examples.cn: 夏日傍晚乐手们摆开摊子，广场就热闹起来。

examples.en: The pond was alive with dragonflies after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后池塘里到处是蜻蜓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊来夫」——耳边一声「啊，来了」，说明人还有气：活着、有生气。

root: 古英语短语 on life 的缩合：on 表示「在……之中」，lif 即 life「生命」，合起来是「在生命之中」，中古英语写作 alife，后定型为 alive。词首 a- 来自介词 on，与 asleep、awake 同一模式；前置定语的位置后来让给了 living。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses follow one movement: the warmth of life staying in a body, showing as energy, lasting in things, spilling into a crowded place, sharpening into attention, and waking a whole scene.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项沿着同一个动作展开：生命的热度留在身体里、显现为精力、延续在事物中、溢满一处地方、锐化成注意力，最后唤醒整个场景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warmth and breath stay inside a body, and the body keeps moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：热气和呼吸还留在身体里，身体仍在动。

branches.en: THE BODY: life has not left, so the creature is not dead.
branches.cn: 身体线：生命没有离开，所以生物没有死。

branches.en: THE SPARK: the same life shows as energy in a person and as movement in a scene.
branches.cn: 火花线：同一种生命，在人身上表现为精力，在场景中表现为动静。

branches.en: THE TRADITION: a custom still in life has not died out.
branches.cn: 传统线：仍在「生命里」的习俗没有消亡。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a place full of creatures borrows the life that fills it.
branches.cn: 场所线：满是生物的地方，借来了充满其中的那份生命。

branches.en: THE MIND: to be alive to something is to be awake to it.
branches.cn: 心智线：对某物 alive，就是对其保持醒觉。

intro.en: Alive is an English phrase turned into one word; its parts are the preposition on and the noun life, and modern English later adds -ness.
intro.cn: alive 是一个变成一个词的英语短语；成分是介词 on 与名词 life，现代英语后来又加上 -ness。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon behind alive, so the Latin column stays empty; the history is entirely Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: alive 背后没有拉丁语词源，所以拉丁语一栏留空；它的历史完全属于日耳曼语。

items.meaning: in, on, in a state of
items.example: On life meant in life, the phrase behind the whole word.
items.exampleCN: on life 意为「在生命之中」，正是整个词背后的短语。

items.example: Lif is the noun that became modern life.
items.exampleCN: lif 是后来变成现代英语 life 的那个名词。

items.example: The phrase was spoken as two words before it fused.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语在粘合之前是分两个词说的。

items.example: Alife is the middle step between on life and alive.
items.exampleCN: alife 是 on life 与 alive 之间的中间形式。

items.meaning: in, on, worn down from on
items.meaningCN: 在……之中，由 on 磨短而来
items.example: The same a- appears in asleep and awake.
items.exampleCN: 同一个 a- 也出现在 asleep 与 awake 里面。

items.example: It forms aliveness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aliveness。

items.example: Life plus -ly gives lively, a cousin rather than a child of alive.
items.exampleCN: life 加 -ly 得到 lively，它是 alive 的远亲而不是直系派生。

items.meaning: being alive; the attributive partner of alive
items.meaningCN: 活着的；alive 的定语搭档
items.example: Living fills the place before a noun that alive cannot take.
items.exampleCN: living 占据了 alive 无法使用的前置定语位置。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「活力；生机；仍活着的事实」
由同源名词 life 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；生动的」
与本词同出古英语 lif，是这一词族的根词，义为「生命；生活」

definition_zh: 所有的；全部；一切；完全；唯一；比分相同；all in all（总而言之）
definition_en: the whole of a group or mass, everything, completely, the only thing, an equal score, or the summary phrase all in all
core_image: 一张桌上摆满盘子，直到没有一点空处
scene: 考试结束的铃声响起，监考老师让每个人放下笔。All the students handed in their papers at once.
sceneCN: 这里 all 是「所有的」（第 1 个义项：一个群体里的每一个成员）；句意为所有学生同时交了卷。画面里可辨认的是考场、试卷与收卷的篮子。

pos.zh: 限定词：所有的；全部的
代词：一切；全部事物
副词：完全地；在固定短语中表示总结或强调

collocations.zh: 根本；全然（多用于否定与疑问）

derivatives.zh: 由 all 加 most 构成，义为「几乎；差不多」，字面是「差不多全部」
由 all 加 way 的旧形式构成，义为「总是；始终」
由 all 加 so 构成，义为「也；还」
由 all 加 one 构成，义为「独自的；单独的」

senses.title: Every member of a group
senses.definition: each person or thing in a group, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中的每个人或物，合在一起看
senses.example: All the students stood up when the headmaster entered.
senses.exampleCN: 校长进来时，所有学生都站了起来。
senses.why: The Old English word named a whole; to name a whole group is to reach every member at once, so the first sense is each one of them.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eall 指一个完整的整体；一次说到整个群体，就等于一次点到其中每一个成员，所以第一个义项是「全体每一个」。

senses.title: The whole of something
senses.definition: the complete amount or extent of a mass that cannot be counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 不可逐个计数的物质或事物的完整数量与范围
senses.example: He drank all the water in the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把瓶子里的水全喝了。
senses.why: Water has no members to count, so the same whole is seen as one undivided amount rather than as a set of units, which gives the mass sense.
senses.whyCN: 水没有可以逐个计数的成员，于是同一个「整体」被看成一份不可分割的量，而不是一堆单位，这就是物质名词前的「全部、整个」。

senses.title: Everything
senses.definition: everything that exists or is involved, used as a pronoun without a following noun
senses.definitionCN: 存在或涉及的每一样东西，作代词使用，后面不接名词
senses.example: All was quiet in the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 空房子里一片寂静。
senses.why: When no noun follows, the whole stands by itself and means everything there is; the pronoun is the same whole with its noun left out.
senses.whyCN: 后面不接名词时，这个「整体」就自己站着，表示存在的一切；代词用法就是把名词省掉之后的同一个整体。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: entirely, with nothing left out, used before adjectives and prepositions
senses.definitionCN: 整个地、丝毫不剩，用在形容词与介词之前
senses.example: The children were all wet after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，孩子们全都湿透了。
senses.why: A whole with nothing left out becomes the adverb: not partly wet but wet through, the way a whole covers the thing it touches.
senses.whyCN: 整体不剩一点，就转成副词义：不是部分湿，而是湿透了，就像整体把触到的那一面全盖住。

senses.title: The only thing
senses.definition: the single thing or person involved, with nothing else added
senses.definitionCN: 所涉及的唯一的物或人，不再有别的
senses.example: All she wanted was a quiet room and a hot meal.
senses.exampleCN: 她想要的只是一间安静的屋子和一顿热饭。
senses.why: If the group holds only one member, the whole and the only thing coincide, so all can shrink to mean merely this one.
senses.whyCN: 如果那个群体里只有一个成员，整体与唯一就重合了，于是 all 可以缩小为「仅仅是这一个」。

senses.title: Equal in score
senses.definition: with the same score on both sides, as in two all or three all
senses.definitionCN: 双方得分相同，如 two all 或 three all 中的用法
senses.example: The match ended two all after extra time.
senses.exampleCN: 加时赛结束后，比赛以二比二收场。
senses.why: A whole split into two equal shares leaves neither side ahead; the word marks the state in which the two parts together make the complete score.
senses.whyCN: 一个整体被分成相等的两份，谁都不领先；这个词标出的正是两部分合起来恰好是整个比分的状态。

senses.title: In the phrase all in all
senses.definition: in the phrase all in all, meaning when everything has been considered
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 all in all，意为把所有因素都算进去之后
senses.example: All in all, the trip was worth the trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 总的来说，这趟旅行值得费这些周折。
senses.why: The phrase stacks whole upon whole: count everything, then count everything again, and what remains is the overall judgment.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把「整体」叠在「整体」上：把一切算一遍、再算一遍，剩下的就是总的评价，所以 all in all 表示「总而言之」。

intro.en: All is a native Old English word, eall, with cognates across the Germanic languages; only its deeper Indo-European link is uncertain.
intro.cn: all 是英语本族的古英语词 eall，在日耳曼语各语言中都有同源词；只有更早的印欧语联系存疑。

items.en: Eall meant the whole of a group or a mass, and it could stand alone as a pronoun.
items.cn: eall 意为一个群体或一份物质的整体，也可以单独作代词使用。

items.en: The word is generally reconstructed as *allaz, with cognates such as Old Norse allr and Old High German al; a deeper Indo-European etymology has been proposed but remains debated.
items.cn: 一般认为它的原始日耳曼语重构形式是 *allaz，同源词包括古诺斯语 allr 与古高地德语 al；更早的印欧语词源虽有假说，仍有争议。

items.en: Middle English all kept the same range: a whole group, a whole mass, and everything taken together.
items.cn: 中古英语 all 保留了同样的范围：整个群体、整份物质，以及合在一起的一切。

items.en: Compound adverbs with all as their first element, such as almost, always and also, became fixed in this period.
items.cn: 以 all 为第一成分的复合副词，如 almost、always、also，在这一时期固定下来。

items.en: All settles into determiner, pronoun and adverb uses, while idioms such as all in all and after all carry the old whole into fixed phrases.
items.cn: all 稳定为限定词、代词与副词三种用法，而 all in all、after all 这类习语把古老的「整体」带进了固定短语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds whose first element is all; the near-meaning group gathers words that also speak of a complete quantity.
note.cn: 形近组收以 all 为第一成分的复合词；近义组收同样表示完整数量的词。

entries.definition: The adverb for nearly, built from all plus most and meaning not quite all.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「几乎」，由 all 加 most 构成，字面是「差一点就是全部」。

entries.definition: The adverb for at every time, originally all plus a form of way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「总是」，原由 all 加 way 的旧形式构成。

entries.definition: The adverb for in addition, built from all plus so.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「也、还」，由 all 加 so 构成。

entries.definition: Being by oneself, from all plus one, that is, a whole of one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独自的」，由 all 加 one 构成，字面是「整整一个」。

entries.definition: Entirely, or counting everyone together, from all plus together.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地、总共」，由 all 加 together 构成。

entries.definition: One complete thing with no part missing; it stresses unity where all stresses coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「整个的、整体」，强调不可分割的统一，而 all 强调覆盖到每一部分。

entries.definition: Complete and undivided, a more formal word for the whole amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全部的、完整的」，比 all 正式，指完整的量。

entries.definition: Each member of a group looked at one by one; the distributive partner of all.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「每一个」，把群体成员逐一来看，是 all 的分配式搭档。

entries.definition: All things taken together as a single idea; the pronoun all often replaces it.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「一切事物」，把所有东西合为一个概念，常可与代词 all 互换。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English eall and the compounds and idioms that English actually built from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 eall，以及英语确实用它造出的复合词与习语。

normal.en: Eall is the old whole: one word for a complete group or a complete mass.
normal.cn: eall 就是古老的「整体」：一个词包住整个群体或整份物质。

normal.en: As a determiner all points at every member; as a pronoun it stands alone and means everything.
normal.cn: 作限定词时 all 指向每一个成员；作代词时它独自站着，表示一切。

normal.en: Almost, always, also, alone and altogether all begin with the same all.
normal.cn: almost、always、also、alone、altogether 都以同一个 all 开头。

normal.en: Before an adjective all turns into completely, as in all wet or all alone.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前，all 就变成「完全地」，如 all wet、all alone。

normal.en: All in all stacks the whole twice, which is why the phrase ends in a summary.
normal.cn: all in all 把「整体」叠了两次，所以这个短语最后落在总结上。

abstract.en: Picture a table covered with plates until no empty space is left: that is all.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子摆满盘子，直到没有一处空位：这就是 all。

abstract.en: Now sweep everything into one pile, and the pile stands alone as the pronoun.
abstract.cn: 再把所有东西扫成一堆，这堆东西独自站着，就是代词用法。

abstract.en: Then pour the pile over one object until it is buried: the same whole becomes completely.
abstract.cn: 最后把这堆东西倒在一个物体上，直到把它埋住：同一个整体就变成了「完全地」。

examples.en: All the students handed in their papers at once.
examples.cn: 所有学生同时交了卷。

examples.en: He drank all the water in the bottle.
examples.cn: 他把瓶子里的水全喝了。

examples.en: All in all, the trip was worth the trouble.
examples.cn: 总的来说，这趟旅行值得费这些周折。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥」——桌上一声「噢」，盘子已经摆满，一个空位都不剩：全部。

root: 古英语 eall「整体、全部」，与古诺斯语 allr、古高地德语 al 同源，一般认为出自原始日耳曼语的重构形式 *allaz；更早的印欧语联系有假说但仍有争议，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses all begin with one whole: a whole group, a whole mass, everything standing alone, a whole covering, a whole of one, a whole split evenly, and a whole counted twice in a summary phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都从同一个「整体」出发：整个群体、整份物质、独自成立的一切、完整覆盖、只有一员、平均分成两份，以及在总结短语里算了两遍的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table is covered with plates until no empty space is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子被盘子摆满，不留一点空处。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a whole group is reached member by member.
branches.cn: 群体线：整个群体被逐个成员地覆盖到。

branches.en: THE MASS: an uncountable substance is taken as one undivided amount.
branches.cn: 物质线：不可数的物质被当作一份不可分割的量。

branches.en: THE STANDING WHOLE: with no noun it means everything, and with one member it means only that one.
branches.cn: 独立线：不带名词时指一切，只剩一个成员时指那唯一的一个。

branches.en: THE COVERING: a whole laid over an adjective turns into completely.
branches.cn: 覆盖线：整体盖在形容词上，就变成「完全地」。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: a whole split evenly gives an equal score, and a whole counted twice gives a summary.
branches.cn: 账目线：整体平均分开就是平局，整体算两遍就是总结。

intro.en: All is a native English element; the family is built by compounding it with other English words rather than by adding Latin affixes.
intro.cn: all 是英语本族成分；这一词族靠与其他英语词复合而成，而不是靠加拉丁语词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for all, so the Latin column stays empty; the cognates are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: all 没有拉丁语来源，所以拉丁语一栏留空；它的同源词都在日耳曼语中。

items.example: Eall is the recorded Old English form of the word.
items.exampleCN: eall 是这个词有记录的古英语形式。

items.meaning: all, as the first element of compounds
items.meaningCN: 全部，用作复合词的第一成分
items.example: The shorter al- appears in almost and also.
items.exampleCN: 较短的 al- 出现在 almost 与 also 里。

items.example: All plus most gives almost.
items.exampleCN: all 加 most 得到 almost。

items.example: All plus a form of way gives always.
items.exampleCN: all 加 way 的旧形式得到 always。

items.example: All plus so gives also.
items.exampleCN: all 加 so 得到 also。

items.meaning: by oneself, a whole of one
items.example: All plus one gives alone.
items.exampleCN: all 加 one 得到 alone。

items.example: All plus together gives altogether.
items.exampleCN: all 加 together 得到 altogether。

items.example: It turns all into almost in the sense of nearly all.
items.exampleCN: 它使 all 带上「几乎全部」的意思，构成 almost。

由 all 加 way 的旧形式构成，义为「总是；始终」
