definition_zh: 允许；准许；留出（时间、钱）；承认；使有可能；考虑到；给予
definition_en: to permit something, to set aside time or money, to admit that something is true, to make something possible, to take into account, or to grant something
core_image: 原本拦着的手挪开，让人从门口过去
scene: 车站的售票口前，有人牵着一只小狗准备上车。The ticket inspector would not allow dogs on the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 allow 是「允许、准许」（第 1 个义项：准许某人做某事或进入某处）；句意为检票员不允许狗上公交车。画面里可辨认的是车门、牵绳与检票夹。

pos.zh: 及物动词：允许；准许；留出；承认；使有可能；给予
不及物动词：容许（用于 allow of 等结构）

collocations.phrase: allow an hour for the journey

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可允许的；法律上认可的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「津贴；限额；免税额」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「驳回；不准；判为无效」

senses.title: To permit someone to do something
senses.definition: to give permission for someone to do something or to go somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 准许某人做某事或进入某处
senses.example: The librarian allowed us to keep the books for another week.
senses.exampleCN: 图书管理员允许我们把书再借一周。
senses.why: The word came into English from Old French with the sense of approving something; to approve of an act is to let it happen, so approval turns into permission.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古法语进入英语时带有「认可、赞同」的意思；认可一个行为，就是让它发生，于是「赞同」变成了「准许」。

senses.title: To set aside time or money
senses.definition: to plan to give a particular amount of time, money or space to something
senses.definitionCN: 计划把一定量的时间、金钱或空间留给某事
senses.example: Allow an hour to get through security at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 在机场过安检要留出一小时。
senses.why: The allotting branch of the old verb survives here: the amount is marked out in advance and handed to a purpose, the way a portion is allotted.
senses.whyCN: 古老动词里「分配」的那条义线在这里保留下来：数量被事先划出来、交给某个用途，就像分出一份配额。

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept or admit that a fact, claim or quality is true
senses.definitionCN: 接受或承认某个事实、说法或性质是真的
senses.example: She allowed that the plan had one serious weakness.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划有一个严重缺陷。
senses.why: To approve of a statement is to concede that it stands; the old sense of praise softens into the quieter act of granting a point.
senses.whyCN: 认可一个说法，就是承认它站得住；古老的「称赞」义淡化成一种较轻的动作：让这一步、认下这一点。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.titleCN: 使有可能；容许（客观条件）
senses.definition: to make something possible or to let it happen without being stopped
senses.definitionCN: 使某事成为可能，或让它不受阻拦地发生
senses.example: The wide gap in the wall allows water to drain away.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上的大缺口让水能够排出去。
senses.why: When a wall stops blocking, it gives the water permission in a figurative way; the same gate image is applied to conditions rather than to people.
senses.whyCN: 墙不再拦着，就等于以一种比喻的方式给水「放行」；同一幅开门让路的画面，从人身上移到了客观条件上。

senses.title: To take into account
senses.definition: to include a factor in a plan or calculation, used in the phrase allow for
senses.definitionCN: 把某个因素纳入计划或计算，用于 allow for 这一短语
senses.example: We must allow for delays caused by the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须把天气造成的延误考虑进去。
senses.why: Setting aside an amount and setting aside a factor are the same gesture: room is made in advance, so the plan is not thrown off later.
senses.whyCN: 留出一笔数量与留出一个因素本是同一个动作：事先腾出地方，计划以后就不会被这一点打乱。

senses.title: To leave room for a possibility
senses.definition: to make a certain interpretation or action possible, used in the phrase allow of
senses.definitionCN: 使某种解释或做法成为可能，用于 allow of 这一短语
senses.example: The evidence allows of only one explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据只容许一种解释。
senses.why: Here permission becomes room: a set of facts opens one door and closes the others, so what it allows is what it leaves possible.
senses.whyCN: 这里「准许」变成了「余地」：一组事实打开一扇门、关上其余的门，所以它 allow of 的，就是它留下来的可能性。

senses.title: To grant a sum or a reduction
senses.definition: to give someone a particular amount, reduction or right, especially in business or official use
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人一定数额、折扣或权利，多用于商业或公务语境
senses.example: The shop allowed us ten percent off the damaged table.
senses.exampleCN: 店家给那张有破损的桌子打了九折。
senses.why: The allotting sense becomes concrete again: a portion of money is marked off and handed over, so the verb means granting a sum.
senses.whyCN: 「分配」义再次具体化：一笔钱被划出来、交到对方手里，于是动词表示「给予、准予」一笔数额。

intro.en: Allow came through Old French from Latin, and it is generally thought to blend two different Latin verbs; the story is set out below.
intro.cn: allow 经由古法语来自拉丁语，一般认为它混合了两个不同的拉丁语动词；下面分段说明。

items.en: Allaudare, from ad- plus laudare 'to praise', meant to praise or approve of something.
items.cn: allaudare 由 ad- 加 laudare「称赞」构成，意为称赞、认可某事。

items.en: Allocare, from ad- plus locare 'to place', meant to allot or assign something to a person or purpose.
items.cn: allocare 由 ad- 加 locare「放置」构成，意为把某物分配、划拨给某个人或某个用途。

items.en: In Old French the two verbs fell together in form as alouer, which carried both praise and allotment; this merging is generally accepted, though the details are debated.
items.cn: 在古法语中，这两个动词在形式上合流为 alouer，同时带着「称赞」与「分配」两层意思；这一合流一般认为成立，具体细节仍有讨论。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as alowen, meaning to praise, approve, permit, and also to assign or grant.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个词作 alowen，意为称赞、认可、准许，也表示分配与给予。

items.en: The permission sense wins the centre, while allotment survives in allow an hour and allow for, and approval survives in the formal allow that.
items.cn: 「准许」义占据中心，而「分配」义保留在 allow an hour 与 allow for 里，「认可」义则保留在正式的 allow that 结构中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on allow with ordinary suffixes and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers verbs about permission and possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收由 allow 加普通后缀构成的词，以及一个只是长得像的词；近义组收表示准许与可能性的动词。

entries.definition: A sum of money or an amount permitted; formed from allow plus the noun suffix -ance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「津贴、限额」，由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成。

entries.definition: Permitted by rules or law; formed from allow plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可允许的、法定的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: To refuse to accept or permit something, formed with the negative prefix dis-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驳回、不准」，由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: In a voice loud enough to be heard; it only looks like allow, being built from a- plus loud, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「出声地」，只是拼写与 allow 相近，词源不同，由 a- 加 loud 构成。

entries.definition: To give official or formal permission; often more authoritative than allow.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「许可、准许」，多带官方或正式色彩，语气比 allow 更强。

entries.definition: To allow something to happen, used mostly in speech and followed by a bare verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「让、允许」，多用于口语，后面直接跟不带 to 的动词。

entries.definition: To make someone able to do something; it points at capacity rather than permission.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」，强调能力而不是许可，与 allow 表示「使有可能」的义项最近。

entries.definition: To give official power or approval for an action; formal and institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「授权、批准」，语气正式，带有机构色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French and Latin history of the word, together with the frames it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的古法语与拉丁语来历，以及它实际出现的句式。

normal.en: Latin laudare is to praise: allow began as approving something, and approval turned into permission.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 laudare 是「称赞」：allow 原先是「认可」，认可又转成「准许」。

normal.en: Latin locare is to place: the allotting branch gives allow an hour and allow for.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 locare 是「放置」：分配这条义线给出 allow an hour 与 allow for。

normal.en: Allow somebody to do something is the plain permission frame; allow plus a bare object is rarer.
normal.cn: allow somebody to do something 是最基本的准许句式；allow 后面只接宾语的情况较少。

normal.en: Allow for is to leave room in a plan; allow of is to leave room in an interpretation.
normal.cn: allow for 是在计划里留出余地；allow of 是在解释上留出余地。

normal.en: The negative prefix dis- makes disallow, the official word for turning a request down.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 dis- 构成 disallow，是正式驳回请求的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand at a doorway: the palm turns, and the person behind it may pass.
abstract.cn: 想象门口举起的一只手：手掌一转，后面的人就可以过去。

abstract.en: The same hand also marks off a portion of time, pushing an hour aside for the journey.
abstract.cn: 同一只手也在划出一段时间，把一小时推到一边留给路程。

abstract.en: When a wall rather than a person opens, the gesture becomes possibility: the gap allows water through.
abstract.cn: 当打开的是墙而不是人，这个动作就变成可能性：缺口让水流过去。

examples.en: The librarian allowed us to keep the books for another week.
examples.cn: 图书管理员允许我们把书再借一周。

examples.en: Allow an hour to get through security at the airport.
examples.cn: 在机场过安检要留出一小时。

examples.en: We must allow for delays caused by the weather.
examples.cn: 我们必须把天气造成的延误考虑进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额老」——门口老人一点头，抬手放人过去：准许；也指先划出一份留给人。

root: 古法语 alouer，一般认为混合了两个拉丁语动词：allaudare「称赞、认可」由 ad- 加 laudare「称赞」构成，allocare「分配、划拨」由 ad- 加 locare「放置」构成。合流之后，认可义发展为准许，分配义保留在「留出」与「给予」的用法里。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses follow one gesture: a hand lifts at a door, and the same lifting becomes permission, a portion set aside, a point conceded, a condition opened, a factor counted in, room for an interpretation, and a sum granted.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项沿着同一个动作展开：门口的手抬起，这一抬就成了准许、划出一份、认下一点、打开条件、算进因素、留下解释余地，以及给予一笔数额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that was blocking a doorway turns and lets someone pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本拦在门口的手一转，放人过去。

branches.en: THE GATE: approval of an act becomes permission to do it.
branches.cn: 门线：对一个行为的认可，变成做这件事的准许。

branches.en: THE PORTION: a share of time or money is marked off and handed over.
branches.cn: 份额线：一段时间或一笔钱被划出来并交出去。

branches.en: THE POINT: approving a claim becomes conceding that it is true.
branches.cn: 论点线：认可一种说法，变成承认它为真。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: a gap that stops blocking lets things happen by themselves.
branches.cn: 条件线：不再阻挡的缺口，让事情自行发生。

branches.en: THE MARGIN: room left in a plan is allow for, room left in meaning is allow of.
branches.cn: 余量线：计划里留下的余地是 allow for，含义上留下的余地是 allow of。

intro.en: Allow is a Latin verb reshaped by Old French, and English then adds its own suffixes to build the family.
intro.cn: allow 是经古法语改造的拉丁语动词，英语再用自己的后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The two Latin verbs behind the word are both recorded, though their merger in Old French is reconstructed from later forms rather than documented step by step.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后的两个拉丁语动词都有记录，但它们在古法语中的合流是根据后来的形式推知的，并没有逐字的文献记录。

items.exampleCN: 它同时出现在 allaudare 与 allocare 的开头。

items.example: Laudare supplies the approving side of the word.
items.exampleCN: laudare 提供了这个词「认可」的那一面。

items.example: Locare supplies the allotting side of the word.
items.exampleCN: locare 提供了这个词「分配」的那一面。

items.example: It is one of the two sources of the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是现代这个动词的两个来源之一。

items.example: It is the other source of the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是现代这个动词的另一个来源。

items.example: Alouer is the form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: alouer 是英语借入的那个形式。

items.example: It forms allowable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 allowable。

items.example: It forms allowance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 allowance。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 disallow。

definition_zh: 津贴；补助；零花钱；限额；免税额；折让；体谅
definition_en: a regular sum of money given for a purpose, pocket money, a permitted amount, a tax-free amount, a price reduction, or the act of taking something into account
core_image: 一只手里预先分好的一小叠钱，只够用在说好的地方
scene: 机场值机柜台前，行李箱刚放上秤，指针就超出了刻度。Her suitcase was five kilos over the baggage allowance.
sceneCN: 这里 allowance 是「限额、允许量」（第 3 个义项：规定可以携带或使用的数量）；句意为她的行李箱超出托运行李限额五公斤。画面里可辨认的是秤、行李箱与值机柜台。

pos.zh: 名词：津贴；零花钱；限额；免税额；折让；体谅

collocations.zh: 同业折让；以旧换新折价

senses.title: A regular sum for a purpose
senses.definition: a fixed sum of money paid regularly to someone for a particular purpose, such as travel or housing
senses.definitionCN: 为某一用途定期付给某人的固定款项，如交通或住房
senses.example: The company pays a travel allowance to staff who work away from home.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给在外地工作的员工发放差旅津贴。
senses.why: Allow first meant to allot a portion; the noun names that allotted portion, and when the portion is paid regularly for a stated purpose it becomes an allowance.
senses.whyCN: allow 最初有「分出一份」的意思；名词就指分出的那一份，当这一份是按期支付、用途固定时，就成了「津贴、补助」。

senses.title: Pocket money for a child
senses.definition: a small sum of money given to a child regularly, usually by a parent
senses.definitionCN: 定期给孩子的一小笔钱，通常由父母给
senses.example: He saves half of his weekly allowance for a new bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每周零花钱的一半存起来，想买辆新自行车。
senses.why: This is the allotted portion at its smallest and most personal: the parent marks off a share and hands it over, and the child may spend it.
senses.whyCN: 这是「分出一份」最小、最贴近生活的形态：父母划出一小份交给孩子，由孩子自己花用。

senses.title: A permitted amount
senses.definition: the amount of something that is officially permitted, such as weight, luggage or time
senses.definitionCN: 官方允许的数量，如重量、行李或时间
senses.example: Each passenger has a baggage allowance of twenty kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 每位乘客的行李限额是二十公斤。
senses.why: Permission measured becomes a quantity: the verb allows up to a limit, and the noun is that limit turned into a figure you can weigh.
senses.whyCN: 把「准许」量化，就成了一个数目：动词允许到某个界限，名词就是把这个界限变成一个可以称量的数字。

senses.title: An amount free of tax
senses.definition: an amount of income that is not taxed, or that may be earned before tax is paid
senses.definitionCN: 不需纳税的收入额度，或在缴税前可以赚到的额度
senses.example: Every taxpayer receives a basic personal allowance.
senses.exampleCN: 每位纳税人都享有基本个人免税额。
senses.why: The tax office allots a tax-free portion before it starts to count income: the permitted amount is money the state agrees to leave alone.
senses.whyCN: 税务部门在开始计算收入之前先划出一份免税的额度：这个被允许留下的数目，就是国家同意不去动的那部分钱。

senses.title: A reduction in price
senses.definition: a sum taken off a price, often for a trade-in, a fault or an old debt
senses.definitionCN: 从价格中减去的金额，常因以旧换新、瑕疵或旧账而给
senses.example: The dealer offered a generous allowance for the old car.
senses.exampleCN: 车商为那辆旧车给了一笔可观的折价。
senses.why: The allotted portion now moves the other way: instead of money paid out to you, it is money the seller agrees not to charge.
senses.whyCN: 分出的那一份这次朝反方向走：不是付给你的钱，而是卖方同意不收的那部分钱。

senses.title: In the phrase make allowance for
senses.definition: in the phrase make allowance for, to take a difficulty or a fault into account and judge less harshly
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 make allowance for，指把困难或过失考虑进去，从宽判断
senses.example: We should make allowance for the fact that she is still learning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应当体谅她还在学习这一点。
senses.why: To allow is to leave room; making allowance for someone is leaving room in your judgment for their circumstances, so the noun turns into a mild, human form of permitting.
senses.whyCN: allow 就是留出余地；为某人 make allowance，就是在判断里为他的处境留出余地，于是这个名词变成一种温和、带人情味的「允许」。

intro.en: Allowance is not a Latin noun handed down whole: English built it from its own verb allow plus the suffix -ance, on a pattern already present in Old French.
intro.cn: allowance 不是原封不动传下来的拉丁语名词：它是英语用自己的动词 allow 加后缀 -ance 造出来的，而这一构词模式在古法语中已存在。

items.en: The Latin verbs allaudare 'to praise' and allocare 'to allot' stand behind the verb; only the second supplies the idea of a portion.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 allaudare「称赞」与 allocare「分配」是那个动词的来源；其中只有后者提供了「一份」的概念。

items.en: Old French alouer carried approval and allotment together, and a related noun aloance is recorded with the sense of approval and allocation.
items.cn: 古法语 alouer 同时带着认可与分配两层意思，相关的名词 aloance 有记录，义为认可与分配。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as allowen, and the sense to allot a share was already alive in Middle English.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词作 allowen，而「分出一份」的意思在中古英语时期就已经存在。

items.en: The noun allowaunce appears in the fourteenth century, formed with -ance; exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 allowaunce 见于十四世纪，由后缀 -ance 构成；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun splits into money senses and measuring senses: a sum paid regularly, pocket money, a permitted amount, a tax-free part, a price reduction, and the phrase make allowance for.
items.cn: 这个名词分成「钱」与「量」两条线：定期给付的款项、零花钱、允许的数量、免税部分、减价，以及短语 make allowance for。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same allow family and one that merely resembles it; the near-meaning group gathers sums, limits and reductions that allowance can name.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 allow 词族的词，以及一个只是长得像的词；近义组收 allowance 可能指称的款项、额度与减价。

entries.definition: The verb that allowance is built from, meaning to permit, to set aside or to grant.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「允许、留出、给予」，正是 allowance 由之构成的动词。

entries.definition: Permitted by rules or by law, especially of costs and claims.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可允许的、法定的」，多用于费用与索赔。

entries.definition: To refuse to allow a claim, a goal or a piece of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驳回、判为无效」，用于索赔、进球或证据。

entries.definition: Distant and unfriendly; it only looks and sounds a little like allowance, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「冷淡的、疏远的」，只是拼写与读音略近，词源与 allowance 不同。

entries.definition: Money paid by a government to support a service or a price; wider and more official than allowance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补贴」，由政府出资支持某项服务或价格，比 allowance 更宽、更官方。

entries.definition: A fixed regular payment, especially to a student, a priest or an intern.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「定期津贴」，多指发给学生、神职人员或实习生的固定款项。

entries.definition: A fixed share or a maximum number officially allowed; close to the permitted-amount sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「配额、定额」，指固定的份额或官方允许的上限，与「限额」义最近。

entries.definition: Money returned after a payment, close to the reduction sense of allowance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「退款、回扣」，与 allowance 表示「折让」的义项接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real history of the suffix -ance and the fixed phrases the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用后缀 -ance 的真实来历，以及这个名词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Allow plus -ance makes a noun of the act: what is allowed becomes a thing you can count.
normal.cn: allow 加 -ance 把动作变成名词：被允许的东西成了一个可以计数的物件。

normal.en: The oldest layer is allotment, so an allowance is always a portion marked off in advance.
normal.cn: 最古老的一层是「分配」，所以 allowance 永远是一份事先划出来的份额。

normal.en: Housing allowance and travel allowance are sums paid for a stated purpose.
normal.cn: housing allowance 与 travel allowance 是为明确用途支付的款项。

normal.en: Baggage allowance measures weight, tax allowance measures untaxed income: the same word for two kinds of limit.
normal.cn: baggage allowance 量的是重量，tax allowance 量的是免税收入：同一个词管两种上限。

normal.en: Make allowance for is the human phrase: leave room in your judgment for someone's difficulty.
normal.cn: make allowance for 是最有人情味的用法：在判断里为别人的难处留出余地。

abstract.en: Picture a small stack of notes set apart on a table, already promised to one purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上单独放着一小叠钱，早已许诺给某一个用途。

abstract.en: The stack can also be a weight on a scale: a figure that says how much may pass.
abstract.cn: 这一叠也可以是秤上的一个重量：一个说明能放过去多少的数字。

abstract.en: And it can be empty space in a judgment, the room you leave for someone who is still learning.
abstract.cn: 它还可以是判断里的空白，是你留给一个仍在学习的人的余地。

examples.en: The company pays a travel allowance to staff who work away from home.
examples.cn: 公司给在外地工作的员工发放差旅津贴。

examples.en: Each passenger has a baggage allowance of twenty kilos.
examples.cn: 每位乘客的行李限额是二十公斤。

examples.en: We should make allowance for the fact that she is still learning.
examples.cn: 我们应当体谅她还在学习这一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额老恩斯」——老人按月数出一小叠，只准用在该用的地方：津贴、限额。

root: 由动词 allow 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，最早见于中古英语；allow 出自古法语 alouer，一般认为混合了拉丁语 allaudare「称赞、认可」与 allocare「分配、划拨」。因此 allowance 的核心是「被分出来、被允许的那一份」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all name a portion that has been marked off: money paid for a purpose, pocket money, a permitted weight, a tax-free amount, a price reduction, and the room left for someone in a judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都在说一份被划出来的份额：为某用途支付的钱、零花钱、允许的重量、免税的额度、减去的价，以及判断中为别人留下的余地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small stack of money is set apart in advance and promised to one purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小叠钱被事先分出来，许诺给某一个用途。

branches.en: THE PURSE: a portion is paid out regularly, to a worker or to a child.
branches.cn: 钱袋线：一份钱被定期付出，给员工，也给孩子。

branches.en: THE SCALE: permission is turned into a weight or a number that may not be passed.
branches.cn: 秤线：准许被换算成一个不能越过的重量或数字。

branches.en: THE TAX OFFICE: part of the income is allotted and left untaxed.
branches.cn: 税务线：收入中有一部分被划出，不去征税。

branches.en: THE PRICE: the portion moves the other way and is money the seller does not charge.
branches.cn: 价格线：这一份朝反方向走，成为卖方不收的那部分钱。

branches.en: THE JUDGMENT: the same room is left for a person's difficulty rather than for weight or money.
branches.cn: 判断线：同样的余地留给一个人的难处，而不是留给重量或金钱。

intro.en: Allowance is an English noun made from a borrowed verb; the suffixes that build its family are ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: allowance 是由借来的动词构成的英语名词；扩展这一词族的后缀都是普通的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verbs behind allow are recorded, while the noun allowance itself is an English formation built on the French pattern.
latinIntro.cn: allow 背后的拉丁语动词都有记录，而 allowance 这个名词本身是英语按法语模式造出来的。

definition_en: very nearly but not completely, close to a number or a time, close to happening, close to none in negative phrases, or close to reaching a goal
core_image: 水已到杯口，只差最后一滴没有溢出
scene: 锅里的汤已经炖了整整一个下午，只差最后一点火候。The soup was almost ready when the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 almost 是「差不多、几乎」（第 1 个义项：程度非常接近某种状态但尚未完全达到）；句意为客人到时汤差不多就好了。画面里可辨认的是汤锅、灶火与汤勺。

pos.zh: 副词：几乎；差不多；将近；差一点

derivatives.zh: 本词的第二成分，义为「最多的；大多数的」，出自古英语 mǣst
由 most 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；大多」，与本词同族
由 all 加 mighty 构成，义为「全能的」，与本词同以 all 为第一成分

senses.title: Very nearly, in degree
senses.definition: very nearly, used before an adjective or a state to say that it is close but not complete
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近，用在形容词或状态之前，表示接近但尚未完全达到
senses.example: The two brothers look almost identical from a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 远远看去，这两兄弟几乎一模一样。
senses.why: The word is all plus most, that is, most of all or nearly all; applied to a quality, it says the quality covers nearly the whole of the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 all 加 most，字面是「几乎全部」；用在一种性质上，就是说这种性质几乎占满了整个对象，所以是「差不多、几乎是」。

senses.title: Close to a number or a time
senses.definition: a little less than a stated number, amount or point in time
senses.definitionCN: 比所说的数目、数量或时间点略少一点
senses.example: She has worked in the same office for almost twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在同一间办公室工作了将近二十年。
senses.why: Nearly all of a count brings the hearer to the very edge of the figure; the same gap that leaves a quality incomplete leaves a number one step short.
senses.whyCN: 「几乎全部」把一个数目推到边缘：让性质差一点完成的那个缺口，同样让数字差一步到点，于是有了「将近」。

senses.title: Close to happening
senses.definition: used about an event that came very close to happening but did not happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事非常接近发生，但最终没有发生
senses.example: I almost dropped the tray on the way to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 我端盘子上桌的路上差点把它摔了。
senses.why: An event can be measured like a distance: it travels nearly the whole way to happening and then stops, so almost marks the miss.
senses.whyCN: 一件事也可以像一段距离那样衡量：它几乎走到了「发生」那里却停住，almost 标出的正是这最后的一点没走到。

senses.title: Close to none, with a negative word
senses.definition: used with never, no, nothing and similar words to mean very close to none
senses.definitionCN: 与 never、no、nothing 等否定词连用，表示非常接近「没有」
senses.example: On winter mornings there is almost no traffic before six.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天的早晨六点以前几乎没有车。
senses.why: If almost means nearly all, then almost no means nearly all of a quantity that is not there; the same measure now stands at the empty end of the scale.
senses.whyCN: 如果 almost 是「几乎全部」，那么 almost no 就是「差一点就全都没有」；同一把尺子这次站在刻度的空端，所以表示「几乎没有」。

senses.title: Close to reaching a goal
senses.definition: close to arriving at a place or finishing a task, especially in the fixed phrase almost there
senses.definitionCN: 接近抵达某处或完成某事，尤用于固定说法 almost there
senses.example: Keep going for ten more minutes and we are almost there.
senses.exampleCN: 再走十分钟，我们就快到了。
senses.why: Distance also measures progress: when a task or a journey is nearly all done, almost there reports the last short stretch before arrival.
senses.whyCN: 距离也可以量进度：当一项任务或一段路几乎做完走完时，almost there 报告的正是抵达前最后那一小段。

intro.en: Almost is a native English compound of two Old English words, all and most, and its history is fully recorded from the Old English period onward.
intro.cn: almost 是由两个古英语词 all 与 most 构成的英语本族复合词，自中古英语以前就有完整记录。

items.en: Eall meant the whole of a group or a mass, and it could also stand alone as a pronoun.
items.cn: eall 意为一个群体或一份物质的整体，也可以单独作代词。

items.en: Mæst meant most or greatest, the superlative of the idea of much.
items.cn: mǣst 意为「最多、最大」，是表示「多」这一概念的最高级。

items.en: Eall plus mæst made eallmæst, literally most of all or nearly all, recorded as an adverb meaning almost.
items.cn: eall 加 mǣst 构成 eallmæst，字面是「几乎全部」，有记录作副词，意为「几乎」。

items.en: Middle English shortened the form to almest; the later -most spelling grew by association with the separate word most, and this influence is generally accepted rather than certain in every detail.
items.cn: 中古英语把形式缩短为 almest；后来的 -most 拼写是受独立的词 most 影响而长出来的，这一影响一般认为成立，具体细节并不完全确定。

items.en: The adverb extends from qualities to numbers, to near-events, to negative phrases such as almost never, and to the fixed almost there.
items.cn: 这个副词从性质扩展到数字、几乎发生的事、almost never 这类否定短语，以及固定的 almost there。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with all or with the same most element; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of approximation and the negative member of the same scale.
note.cn: 形近组收由 all 构成或含有同一 most 成分的词；近义组收表示近似程度的副词，以及同一刻度上的否定一端。

entries.definition: The first element of almost, meaning the whole of a group or mass.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词与代词，义为「全部」，是 almost 的第一成分。

entries.definition: The second element of almost, meaning the greatest part or number.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词与副词，义为「大多数、最多」，是 almost 的第二成分。

entries.definition: Mainly or for the most part, built on most with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「主要地、大多」，由 most 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Having complete power, built like almost from all plus a second element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全能的」，与 almost 一样由 all 加第二成分构成。

entries.definition: The closest synonym; it is preferred before a number or a time in careful British use.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「几乎、将近」，是最接近的同义词，在英式用法中数字与时间前更常用它。

entries.definition: Almost, in effect, used of conditions and results rather than of countable things.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上、几乎」，多用于状况与结果，而不是可数的东西。

entries.definition: Close to a figure but not exact; it allows error on either side, unlike almost.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大约」，表示接近某个数字但不精确，误差可大可小，而 almost 只表示略少。

entries.definition: Only just, almost not at all; it stands at the empty end of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「仅仅、几乎不」，正处在同一刻度的空端，与 almost 相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English compound eallmæst and the frames the adverb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语复合形式 eallmæst，以及这个副词实际出现的句式。

normal.en: Eallmæst is all plus most: nearly all, but not quite all.
normal.cn: eallmæst 就是 all 加 most：几乎是全部，但不是全部。

normal.en: The -most ending came by association with most, which is why the word looks like two English words glued together.
normal.cn: 词尾 -most 是受 most 影响而来，所以这个词看起来像两个英语词粘在一起。

normal.en: Before an adjective almost means nearly; before a number or a time it means just short of that point.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前 almost 是「差不多」；放在数字或时间前是「将近」。

normal.en: Almost never and almost nothing mean very close to none.
normal.cn: almost never 与 almost nothing 都表示非常接近「没有」。

normal.en: Almost fell is a narrow miss: the event came close and then stopped.
normal.cn: almost fell 是一次险险的错过：事情已经逼近，却在最后停住。

abstract.en: Picture a glass filled to the brim, with one last drop missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倒到杯口的杯子，只差最后一滴。

abstract.en: The last drop hangs at the edge but does not fall: that is the almost-event.
abstract.cn: 最后一滴悬在杯沿却没有落下：这就是「差一点发生」的事。

abstract.en: Move the same gap onto a clock, and it becomes five minutes to midnight.
abstract.cn: 把同一个缺口挪到钟面上，它就变成差五分钟到午夜。

examples.en: The soup was almost ready when the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到时，汤差不多就好了。

examples.en: She has worked in the same office for almost twenty years.
examples.cn: 她在同一间办公室工作了将近二十年。

examples.en: I almost missed the last train home.
examples.cn: 我差点没赶上回家的末班车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥某斯特」——杯口最后一滴悬着不掉：几乎满了，还差一点。

root: 古英语 eallmǣst，由 eall「全部」加 mǣst「最多、最大」复合而成，字面是「几乎全部」；中古英语写作 almest，后来 -most 的拼写受独立的词 most 影响而定型。更早的印欧语来源不属于这个词自身的构词问题。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses share one gap: a quality covers nearly everything, a count stops one step short, an event comes close and misses, a quantity stands near zero, and a journey is nearly finished.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共用同一个缺口：性质几乎占满、数目差一步、事情逼近又错过、数量接近零、路程快要走完。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass is filled to the brim, with one last drop still missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子已到杯口，只差最后一滴。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: a property covers nearly the whole of the thing.
branches.cn: 性质线：一种属性几乎占满整个对象。

branches.en: THE COUNT: a figure is reached all but one step.
branches.cn: 数目线：一个数字只差一步就到。

branches.en: THE EVENT: the action travels nearly all the way and stops before happening.
branches.cn: 事件线：动作几乎走完全程，却在发生之前停住。

branches.en: THE EMPTY END: with a negative word the same gap sits next to zero.
branches.cn: 空端线：与否定词连用时，同一个缺口紧挨着零。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: progress is nearly complete, and arrival is one short stretch away.
branches.cn: 路程线：进度接近完成，抵达只剩短短一段。

intro.en: Almost is an English compound, so its parts are Old English words rather than Latin affixes; English suffixes appear only in the wider family.
intro.cn: almost 是英语复合词，成分是古英语的词而不是拉丁词缀；英语后缀只出现在更大的词族里。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element enters almost itself, so the Latin column is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: almost 本身没有拉丁语成分，所以拉丁语一栏留空。

items.example: Eall is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: eall 是这个复合词的第一成分。

items.example: Mæst is the second element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: mǣst 是这个复合词的第二成分。

items.example: Eallmæst is the recorded ancestor of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: eallmæst 是这个词有记录的前身。

items.example: Middle English almest shows the shortened first element.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语的 almest 显示了缩短后的第一成分。

items.meaningCN: 受 most 影响而改写的最高级词尾
items.example: The ending was respelled after the word most.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾在词 most 的影响下被改写。

items.example: All keeps the first half of the compound alive.
items.exampleCN: all 让这个复合词的前半部分沿用至今。

items.example: Most keeps the second half of the compound alive.
items.exampleCN: most 让这个复合词的后半部分沿用至今。

items.example: It forms mostly from most.
items.exampleCN: 它加在 most 后构成 mostly。

items.example: It shows the same all plus second element pattern.
items.exampleCN: 它显示出同样的「all 加第二成分」模式。

derivatives.zh: 本词的第二成分，义为「最多的；大多数的」
由 most 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；大多」
由 all 加 mighty 构成，义为「全能的」，与本词同以 all 为第一成分

definition_zh: 独自的；单独的；单独地；单靠自己；仅仅、只有；独一无二
definition_en: without other people present, without help from anyone, or used to mean only this one and nothing else
core_image: 一盏灯、一把椅子、一个人，墙上没有第二个影子
scene: 深夜的实验室只剩一盏灯，其他人早已离开。She preferred to work alone after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 alone 是「独自一人」（第 1 个义项：身边没有其他人在场）；句意为她喜欢在午夜之后独自工作。画面里可辨认的是长桌、台灯与空着的椅子。

pos.zh: 形容词（多作表语）：独自的；单独的；仅仅的
副词：独自地；单靠自己做；仅仅

forms.label: 形容词原级（只作表语，无比较级与最高级）

derivatives.zh: 由 alone 首音节被误分而反成，义为「单独的；孤独的」
由 lone 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「孤独的、寂寞的」，带主观情绪
由 lonely 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「孤独、寂寞」
由 alone 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「独处的状态」，不带情绪色彩

senses.title: Being the only person present
senses.definition: being in a place with no other person present
senses.definitionCN: 所处之处没有其他人在场
senses.example: She sat alone in the empty waiting room until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自坐在空荡荡的候诊室里，一直等到午夜。
senses.why: Alone is a contraction of all and one: the count of people stops at one, with no second person added. That is why the basic sense is simply that nobody else is here, not necessarily that one feels sad.
senses.whyCN: alone 是 all 与 one 的缩合，字面意思是「数下来全是一个」；人数数到一就停，没有第二个人加进来。所以它的本义只是「身边没有别人」，并不必然带悲伤色彩。

senses.title: Doing something with no help
senses.definition: doing something without help or support from other people
senses.definitionCN: 做某事时没有得到别人的帮助或支持
senses.example: He rebuilt the engine alone, with no manual and no helper.
senses.exampleCN: 他独自重装了发动机，既没有手册，也没有帮手。
senses.why: If the whole count is one person, then the whole work also falls to one pair of hands. The absence of other people is read as the absence of help.
senses.whyCN: 如果整份人数只有一个，那么整件活也只能落到一双手上；「没有别人」被读成「没有帮手」，于是有了「单靠自己」这个义项。

senses.title: Only this one and nothing else
senses.definition: used after a noun or pronoun to mean that this one thing and no other is involved
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词或代词之后，表示涉及的只有这一项，没有别的
senses.example: Money alone will not fix a school that has lost its teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 单靠钱无法让一所失去了教师的学校恢复正常。
senses.why: The same count of one is applied to things instead of people: exclude every other factor, and what is left is the single item, so the word comes to mean only.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「数到一」被从人移到事物上：把其他因素逐一排除，只剩下这一项，词义就变成了正式的「仅仅、只有」。

senses.title: Having no equal
senses.definition: in the phrase stand alone, to be the only one of a kind or to have no equal
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 stand alone，表示同类中仅此一个，或者无人能比
senses.example: As a chronicler of the delta, she stands alone.
senses.exampleCN: 作为三角洲的记述者，她独树一帜。
senses.why: A figure with nobody beside it can be read a second way: nobody can be placed beside it. Loneliness turns into having no equal, which is exactly what stand alone says.
senses.whyCN: 一个身旁没有人的身影还可以换一种读法：没有人能站到它旁边。孤单由此翻成「无人可比」，stand alone 正是这个用法。

senses.title: Let alone: and even less so
senses.definition: in the phrase let alone, used after a negative statement to say that a further case is even less possible
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 let alone，接在否定陈述之后，表示进一步的情况更不可能
senses.example: He could not lift the box, let alone carry it upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 他连箱子都抬不起来，更不用说搬上楼了。
senses.why: Let alone literally means leave it by itself: the harder case is set aside and not even counted, because the easier case has already failed.
senses.whyCN: let alone 字面是「把它单独搁着」：更难的那一项被搁到一边，干脆不列进计数，因为较容易的那一项已经不成立。

senses.title: Leave someone alone: stop disturbing
senses.definition: in the phrase leave someone or something alone, to stop touching, bothering or interfering with it
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 leave someone or something alone，表示不再触碰、打扰或干预
senses.example: Leave the sleeping dog alone and walk quietly past the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 别去惹那条睡着的狗，安静地从门口走过去。
senses.why: To leave a person alone is to keep them in the state of being all one, without adding your presence, your voice or your hands to their business.
senses.whyCN: leave someone alone 就是让人保持「全是一个」的状态，不把自己的身影、声音或手加进去，所以是「别打扰、别插手」。

intro.en: Alone is a native English contraction rather than a borrowed word, and its history explains both the a- at the front and the separate word lone.
intro.cn: alone 不是借词，而是英语本族语的缩合形式；它的历史既能解释词首那个 a，也能解释 lone 这个独立词的由来。

items.en: *ainaz is the reconstructed Germanic word for one, the second element of the compound; the asterisk marks a form rebuilt by comparison rather than a written record.
items.cn: 重构形式 *ainaz 是日耳曼语中表示「一」的词，也是这个复合词的后半；星号表示这是比较得出的重构形式，并非文献记录。

items.en: The phrase al ana meant wholly alone, with al meaning all and ana meaning by oneself; ana itself came from an, one.
items.cn: 短语 al ana 意为「完全独自」，其中 al 表示「全部」，ana 表示「独自」；ana 本身又来自 an「一」。

items.en: The two words were increasingly written together as al one and then alone; the unstressed vowel of the first part weakened and the space disappeared.
items.cn: 两个词逐渐连写成 al one，再变成 alone；前半的弱读元音随之弱化，词间的空格也消失了。

items.en: Writers divided alone wrongly as a lone, and the new adjective lone was born from that mistake; the change is generally dated to the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 文人把 alone 误分为 a lone，新的形容词 lone 就从这次误分中产生；这一变化一般认为发生在十六世纪。

items.en: The sense only is recorded from the fifteenth century, and the fixed phrases let alone and leave alone grew from the same count of one.
items.cn: 「仅仅」这一义项一般认为自十五世纪起有记录；固定说法 let alone 与 leave alone 都从同一个「数到一」的画面长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the word that was cut out of alone, the emotional adjective built on it, and two words that share only the spelling; the near-meaning group holds words about being single, sole or without company.
note.cn: 形近组收从 alone 里误分出来的词、由它构成的情绪形容词，以及两个只是拼写接近的词；近义组收表示单独、唯一与无人陪伴的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning solitary, created when writers read a lone traveller as two words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「单独的、孤独的」，源于把 a lone traveller 误读成两个词，是 alone 的反成词。

entries.definition: Feeling sad because one has no company; alone states a fact, while lonely adds the feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「孤独的、寂寞的」，由 lone 加 -ly 构成；alone 只陈述事实，lonely 添上了情绪。

entries.definition: A preposition and adverb meaning from one end to the other; it merely looks similar and comes from Old English andlang.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「沿着、向前」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自古英语 andlang。

entries.definition: Distant and unfriendly in manner; it merely looks similar and comes from a nautical term for the windward side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「冷淡的、疏远的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自表示上风舷的航海用语。

entries.definition: Done or existing alone, often by choice or by nature; more formal and more deliberate than alone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独自的、独居的」，常含主动选择或天性使然之意，比 alone 更正式。

entries.definition: Being the single one and no more; the direct match for the formal sense of alone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与副词，义为「唯一的、仅仅」，与 alone 的正式义项「仅仅」直接对应。

entries.definition: Travelling or appearing without a companion; a formal word for being alone in public.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无人陪伴的」，是公开场合「独自一人」的正式说法。

entries.definition: Done by one person without help; it matches the second sense of alone almost exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与副词，义为「独自完成的、单枪匹马的」，几乎正好对应 alone 的第二个义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real contraction of all plus one, the mistaken split that produced lone, and the fixed phrases the word actually lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的缩合 all 加 one、误分出来的 lone，以及这个词实际出现的固定说法。

normal.en: All plus one: count the people in the room and stop at one.
normal.cn: all 加 one：数屋里的人，数到一就停。

normal.en: The a at the front is not an article; it is the worn-down remains of all.
normal.cn: 词首的 a 不是冠词，而是 all 磨损后留下的残迹。

normal.en: Lone was cut out of alone by a wrong division, so the two words share one history.
normal.cn: lone 是从 alone 里被错误切分出来的，两个词共用一段历史。

normal.en: Let alone sets the harder case aside: it is not even counted.
normal.cn: let alone 把更难的那一项搁在一边：它根本不被计入。

normal.en: Leave someone alone keeps that person in the state of being all one.
normal.cn: leave someone alone 就是让那个人保持「全是一个」的状态。

abstract.en: One lamp, one chair, one shadow on the wall.
abstract.cn: 一盏灯、一把椅子、墙上一个影子。

abstract.en: A single set of footprints crossing an empty beach, with no second pair behind.
abstract.cn: 一串脚印穿过空海滩，身后没有第二串。

abstract.en: At the end of a chess game only one king is left standing on the board.
abstract.cn: 棋局终了，棋盘上只剩一个王还立着。

examples.en: She lives alone in a small flat above the bakery.
examples.cn: 她独自住在面包店楼上的一间小公寓里。

examples.en: He finished the whole repair alone, without a manual or a helper.
examples.cn: 他独自完成了整场修理，既没有手册，也没有帮手。

examples.en: Money alone cannot rebuild a school that has lost its teachers.
examples.cn: 单靠钱无法重建一所失去了教师的学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿隆」——空屋里只守着一条影子：独自的；也指「仅仅」。

root: 由古英语短语 al ana「完全独自」缩合而成，al 是 all 的旧形，ana「独自」又来自 an「一」。中古英语写作 al one，后拼作 alone；十六世纪又被误分为 a lone，由此产生 lone。一般认为「仅仅」义自十五世纪起有记录。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all rest on one count, all one: the count can describe a room, a pair of hands, a quantity, a rank, or a phrase that keeps other people away.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都建立在同一个计数上：全是一个。这个计数可以指一间屋子、一双手、一个数量、一个地位，也可以指一句把别人挡在外面的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp, one chair, one person, and no second shadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯、一把椅子、一个人，没有第二个影子。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the count of people present is exactly one.
branches.cn: 空间线：在场的人数恰好是一个。

branches.en: THE WORK: with no second pair of hands, the task is finished by one person.
branches.cn: 做事线：没有第二双手，活就由一个人做完。

branches.en: THE QUANTITY: the same count applied to things leaves only one item.
branches.cn: 数量线：同一个计数移到事物上，只剩下一项。

branches.en: THE RANK: nobody can be placed beside the single figure, so it has no equal.
branches.cn: 地位线：无人能站到这个身影旁边，于是无人可比。

branches.en: THE PHRASES: let alone withholds a harder case, and leave alone withholds your presence.
branches.cn: 短语线：let alone 扣住更难的一项，leave alone 扣住你的在场。

intro.en: Alone is a native compound of two Old English words, and English later added ordinary suffixes to build the family around it.
intro.cn: alone 由两个古英语词缩合而成，英语后来再用普通后缀在它周围扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The word itself is Germanic, but Latin unus one descends from the same Indo-European root, so a few Latin cognates can be listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身属日耳曼语，但拉丁语 unus「一」出自同一个印欧词根，所以可以在这里列出几个拉丁同源词。

items.example: The first element of the compound means the whole of something.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词的第一部分表示某物的全部。

items.example: The numeral is the second element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个数词是复合词的第二部分。

items.example: It gave the phrase its sense of being on one's own.
items.exampleCN: 它把「靠自己一个人」的意思带给了这个短语。

items.meaning: all, as written before a consonant
items.meaningCN: all 在中古英语中的写法
items.example: It appears in the two-word spelling al one.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在分写的 al one 这一形式里。

items.structure: English adjective from a wrong division
items.example: It was split off from alone in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 它在十六世纪从 alone 里被切分出来。

items.example: It forms lonely from lone.
items.exampleCN: 它由 lone 构成 lonely。

items.example: It forms aloneness and loneliness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aloneness 与 loneliness。

items.meaning: the article a read into alone
items.meaningCN: 被误读进 alone 的冠词 a
items.example: A lone traveller is really alone plus a traveller.
items.exampleCN: a lone traveller 实际是 alone 加上 traveller。

definition_zh: 沿着；顺着；向前；一道、随行；连同（along with）；自始至终（all along）；相处、进展（get along）
definition_en: from one end of something towards the other, onwards, or together with someone or something
core_image: 一根手指贴着一条长线，从这头一直划到那头
scene: 雨后的乡间小路上，两个人并肩慢慢往村口走。We walked along the river until the bridge came into sight.
sceneCN: 这里 along 是「沿着」（第 1 个义项：从一端顺着走向另一端）；句意为我们沿着河一直走到桥进入视野。画面里可辨认的是河岸、小路与远处的石桥。

pos.zh: 介词：沿着；顺着；在……期间
副词：向前；一道；连同

derivatives.zh: 由 along 加 side 复合而成，义为「在……旁边；与……一起」
由 along 加 shore 复合而成，义为「沿岸的；沿着海岸」
中古英语的旧形式，在 along 后加 -st，义同「沿着」，今已罕见

senses.title: From one end to the other
senses.definition: moving or extending from one end of something towards the other, close to its length
senses.definitionCN: 从某物的一端顺着走向另一端，贴着它的长度移动或延伸
senses.example: We cycled along the canal for an hour before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨之前，我们沿着运河骑了一个小时。
senses.why: Old English andlang was built from and- meaning facing or throughout and lang meaning long: the word literally runs the whole length of a thing, so the preposition means along.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 andlang 由 and-「朝着、贯穿」加 lang「长」构成，字面就是「顺着整条长度走」，所以介词义是「沿着」。

senses.title: Forward or onward
senses.definition: moving forward or continuing on one's way, especially in the phrase move along
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动或继续赶路，尤用于短语 move along
senses.example: The guard asked the crowd to move along and keep the entrance clear.
senses.exampleCN: 保安请人群往前走，保持入口畅通。
senses.why: If you follow a line to its far end, you are already going forward; the whole length of the path turns into a direction of travel, and the adverb means onward.
senses.whyCN: 顺着一条线走到尽头，本身就是在往前；「整条长度」于是变成「行进方向」，副词义就成了「向前、继续走」。

senses.title: Coming or bringing with you
senses.definition: coming with someone or bringing something with you, as in come along or bring along
senses.definitionCN: 与某人同来，或把某物随身带来，如 come along 与 bring along
senses.example: Bring along a notebook, because the guide will not supply paper.
senses.exampleCN: 随身带个本子，因为导游不提供纸张。
senses.why: Travelling the same length as someone means sharing the road with them; along the same path turns into in company with, and that is why bring along means carry it with you.
senses.whyCN: 和别人走同一段路，就是与人同行；「沿同一条路」自然转成「一道、同行」，所以 bring along 是「随身带上」。

senses.title: Along with: together with
senses.definition: in the phrase along with, together with another person or thing, often as an addition
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 along with，表示与另一人或另一物一起，常带「附加」意味
senses.example: Along with two engineers, the team hired a translator.
senses.exampleCN: 团队连同两名工程师一起，还雇了一名译员。
senses.why: Here the shared path is no longer physical: two things are put on the same line of a list and travel together through the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这里共享的不再是真实道路，而是清单上的同一行：两样东西被排在一起、一起进入句子，所以 along with 是「连同、加之」。

senses.title: All along: from the beginning
senses.definition: in the phrase all along, during the whole of a period, from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 all along，表示在某段时间的全部过程中，从头到尾
senses.example: She knew all along that the letter had been opened.
senses.exampleCN: 她自始至终都知道那封信被人拆开过。
senses.why: All adds the whole length to along: not one part of the road but the entire road, so the phrase covers the whole stretch of time.
senses.whyCN: all 把「整段」推到极致：不是路上的一段，而是从头到尾的整条路，所以 all along 表示整段时间「自始至终」。

senses.title: Get along: to be on good terms
senses.definition: in the phrase get along, to have a friendly relationship with someone, or to make progress
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 get along，表示与某人关系融洽，或者事情有所进展
senses.example: The two new roommates get along better than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 两个新室友相处得比谁预料的都好。
senses.why: To get along is to keep moving down the same road without collision; a shared journey that runs smoothly becomes a relationship that runs smoothly.
senses.whyCN: get along 是「同一条路上走得下去、不撞车」；一段顺利的共同路程，就引申为人际关系上的「合得来」。

senses.title: Along the way: during the journey
senses.titleCN: 沿途；在过程中（along the way）
senses.definition: in the phrase along the way, at points during a journey or during a process
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 along the way，表示在旅途中或在某个过程的某些节点上
senses.example: They picked up two stray dogs along the way.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一路上收留了两只流浪狗。
senses.why: The road is now a stretch of events rather than ground: whatever happens at points on that stretch happens along the way.
senses.whyCN: 路在这里成了事件的连续段：在这条线上各处发生的事，就是「沿途、在过程中」发生的。

intro.en: Along is a native compound whose first element is an old prefix meaning facing or throughout and whose second element is simply long.
intro.cn: along 是本族复合词：第一部分是表示「朝着、贯穿」的古老前缀，第二部分就是「长」。

items.en: The prefix is reconstructed as *andi-, toward or facing, and the adjective as *langaz, long; both are starred forms rebuilt by comparison.
items.cn: 前缀一般重构为 *andi-，意为「朝向、面对」；形容词重构为 *langaz，意为「长」；两者都是比较得出的星号形式。

items.en: Andlang meant the whole length of, throughout, built from and- plus lang; German entlang follows the same pattern.
items.cn: andlang 意为「整条长度、贯穿」，由 and- 加 lang 构成；德语 entlang 是同样的构词模式。

items.en: The -d- was lost, giving along; the shorter form is generally recorded from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 词中的 -d- 脱落，形成 along；这一较短形式一般认为自十三世纪起有记录。

items.en: The adverb use for onward or forward and the phrase along with developed in this period; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 副词义「向前」以及 along with 这一说法在这一时期发展出来；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Phrasal uses multiply: all along, get along, come along, and the everyday instruction move along.
items.cn: 短语用法不断增多：all along、get along、come along，以及日常的 move along。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the compound alongside, the shore compound built on the same element, the adjective long inside the word, and a word that only shares the spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for length, side and forward movement.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一成分构成的 alongside 与 alongshore、词内的形容词 long，以及一个只是拼写接近的词；近义组收表示长度、侧旁与向前的词。

entries.definition: A preposition and adverb meaning next to or together with, built from along plus side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「在……旁边、与……一起」，由 along 加 side 复合而成。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning along the shore, built on the same along element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与副词，义为「沿岸的、沿着海岸」，由同一个 along 成分加 shore 构成。

entries.definition: The adjective long is the second element of the Old English compound and gives the word its idea of length.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词 long「长的」是古英语复合词的第二部分，为这个词提供了「长度」的观念。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning without others; it merely looks similar and comes from all plus one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与副词，义为「独自的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自 all 加 one 的缩合。

entries.definition: In the direction of the length of something; the strict spatial sense of along without the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 副词与形容词，义为「纵长地、沿长度方向」，只保留 along 的空间义，不含移动。

entries.definition: At the side of something; it marks position rather than the line of travel.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」，标出位置，而不像 along 那样标出沿线的走向。

entries.definition: Toward the front; the direction sense that along carries in move along.
entries.definitionCN: 副词与形容词，义为「向前」，正是 along 在 move along 里带的那个方向义。

entries.definition: In every part of a place or period; it matches the old andlang sense of the whole length.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「遍及、贯穿」，与 andlang 古老的「整条长度」义相合。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English compound andlang and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的古英语复合词 andlang，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Andlang is and- plus lang: a path measured by its whole length.
normal.cn: andlang 就是 and- 加 lang：一条按整段长度来量的小路。

normal.en: The -d- dropped out on the way from andlang to along.
normal.cn: 从 andlang 到 along，中间的 -d- 掉了。

normal.en: German entlang keeps the same shape, so the word is native Germanic.
normal.cn: 德语 entlang 保持同样的形状，可见这个词是日耳曼语本族词。

normal.en: All along means for the entire length of time, not just part of it.
normal.cn: all along 指整段时间的全部，而不只是其中一段。

normal.en: Get along is to keep moving on the same road without collision.
normal.cn: get along 就是在同一条路上继续走而不撞车。

abstract.en: A finger runs down a ruler from the first mark to the last.
abstract.cn: 一根手指顺着尺子，从第一个刻度划到最后一个。

abstract.en: Two walkers share one narrow path, side by side for the whole way.
abstract.cn: 两个人共用一条窄路，整段路都并排走着。

abstract.en: The path keeps going after the walkers stop, because the line is longer than the journey.
abstract.cn: 行人停下之后路还在往前，因为线比行程更长。

examples.en: We cycled along the canal for an hour before the rain came.
examples.cn: 下雨之前，我们沿着运河骑了一个小时。

examples.en: Bring along a notebook, because the guide will not supply paper.
examples.cn: 随身带个本子，因为导游不提供纸张。

examples.en: She knew all along that the letter had been opened.
examples.cn: 她自始至终都知道那封信被人拆开过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿朗」——手指贴着长线一路往前划：沿着；向前；也指「一道」。

root: 古英语 andlang「整条长度、贯穿」，由 and-「朝着、贯穿」加 lang「长」构成，与德语 entlang 同型。中古英语丢掉 -d- 作 along；副词义「向前」以及 along with、all along、get along 等短语都从「同一条长度」这个画面展开。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses follow one line: start at one end, go to the other, take someone with you, and the same line becomes a stretch of time, a relationship or a whole journey.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项沿同一条线展开：从一端走到另一端，再带上同行的人，同一条线又变成一段时间、一段关系或整段旅程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger runs the whole length of a line, from one end to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指贴着一条线，从这一头划到那一头。

branches.en: THE LINE: the preposition lays a path beside something and follows its whole length.
branches.cn: 线条线：介词在事物旁边铺出一条路，并顺着它的整段长度走。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: following the line to its end is moving forward.
branches.cn: 方向线：顺着线走到尽头，本身就是在往前。

branches.en: THE COMPANY: walking the same length with someone becomes coming along and along with.
branches.cn: 同行线：与人走同一段路，就变成 come along 与 along with。

branches.en: THE STRETCH: the line becomes a stretch of time, covered from beginning to end or at points on the way.
branches.cn: 时段线：线变成一段时间，或从头到尾覆盖，或在沿途某些点上发生。

branches.en: THE RELATION: a shared road that runs smoothly becomes getting along with someone.
branches.cn: 关系线：一条走得顺畅的共同道路，变成与人 get along。

intro.en: Along is built from two Old English pieces, and the same pieces reappear in alongside and alongshore.
intro.cn: along 由两个古英语成分构成，同样的成分又出现在 alongside 与 alongshore 里。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic through and through, with no Latin cognate, so the Latin column stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从头到尾属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语同源词，所以拉丁语一栏留空。

items.example: It supplies the direction inside andlang.
items.exampleCN: 它为 andlang 提供了方向感。

items.example: It gives the compound its idea of length.
items.exampleCN: 它把「长度」的观念带给这个复合词。

items.example: It is the direct ancestor of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 它是现代这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: It appears at the front of alongside and alongshore.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 alongside 与 alongshore 的词首。

items.example: It forms alongside.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alongside。

items.example: It forms alongshore.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alongshore。

items.meaning: an old ending added to adverbs
items.meaningCN: 加在副词后的古老词尾
items.example: It forms the archaic alongst.
items.exampleCN: 它构成古旧的 alongst。

items.example: The form survives only in old texts.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式只保留在旧文本里。

definition_zh: 在……旁边；与……并排；与……一起、与……合作；靠（码头、船舷）边；并存
definition_en: at the side of something, together with someone, or close to the side of a ship or pier
core_image: 两条船的船舷贴得很近，几乎碰在一起
scene: 天还没亮，补给船贴着石砌的岸壁缓缓靠过去。The supply boat came alongside the pier just before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 alongside 是「靠在……边」（第 3 个义项：船或码头旁的贴近位置）；句意为补给船在黎明前靠上了码头。画面里可辨认的是缆绳、石壁与船头的水痕。

pos.zh: 介词：在……旁边；与……一起；靠（船、码头）边
副词：靠过来；在侧旁

derivatives.zh: 由 alongside 加 of 构成的完整形式，美式英语中表示「在……旁边」
由同一 along- 成分加 shore 构成的相关词，义为「沿岸的；沿着海岸」
与 along 同源的旧形式，义为「沿着」，与 alongside 共用 along- 成分

senses.title: Next to the side of something
senses.definition: at or by the side of something, with the two running side by side
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的侧边，两者并行排列
senses.example: A row of poplars grows alongside the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 一排白杨沿着铁路生长。
senses.why: The word joins along and side: the whole length of one thing is laid next to the side of another, so the two edges run parallel.
senses.whyCN: alongside 由 along 与 side 复合：把一样东西的整条长度贴到另一样东西的侧边上，两条边于是并行，这就是「在……旁边」。

senses.title: Working together as a partner
senses.definition: working or acting together with someone, especially as a partner or helper
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起工作或行动，尤指作为伙伴或帮手
senses.example: Nurses worked alongside the doctors through the whole night.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们整夜与医生并肩工作。
senses.why: Two people who walk the same length on the same side are partners; the physical side-by-side becomes cooperation without any change of words.
senses.whyCN: 两个人贴着同一侧、走同一段路，就是并肩；空间上的「并排」不加一字就引申为工作上的「一起、协作」。

senses.title: Close to the side of a ship or pier
senses.definition: in nautical use, close to the side of a ship, a pier or a wharf
senses.definitionCN: 航海用语，指贴近船、码头或突堤的侧边
senses.example: The supply boat came alongside the pier just before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 补给船在黎明前靠上了码头。
senses.why: This is the compound's first home: sailors needed a word for a boat lying against another boat's side, and the ordinary side of a ship supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个复合词最早的落脚处：水手需要形容一条船贴住另一条船的侧边，而船本来就有一个「侧边」，于是这个词先用在码头与船舷上。

senses.title: Adverb: drawing near the side
senses.definition: used as an adverb, close to the side of something, especially of a ship drawing near
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时表示靠近某物的侧边，尤指船靠过来
senses.example: The pilot boat drew alongside and a ladder was lowered.
senses.exampleCN: 引航船靠了过来，一条梯子被放了下去。
senses.why: Drop the object and the word turns into an adverb: the side is still there, but the sentence no longer names what is being approached.
senses.whyCN: 省略宾语后，它就成了副词：侧边仍在，只是句子不再点明贴近的是哪样东西，于是表示「靠过来、在旁边」。

senses.title: Alongside of: the fuller form
senses.definition: in American usage, the fuller form alongside of, used before a noun with the same meaning
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中更完整的形式 alongside of，接名词时意思相同
senses.example: A small shed stood alongside of the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓旁边立着一间小棚屋。
senses.why: English often pairs a preposition with of to make a relation explicit; of adds nothing new but makes the side relation feel complete.
senses.whyCN: 英语常给介词再配一个 of，把关系说死；of 不添新义，只是让「在旁边」这层关系显得完整，于是有了 alongside of。

senses.title: Existing side by side
senses.definition: existing or happening at the same time as something else, without replacing it
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物同时存在或发生，并不取代它
senses.example: Traditional remedies are still used alongside modern drugs in the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 在这家诊所里，传统疗法与现代药物仍并存使用。
senses.why: If two things run on the same length without pushing each other away, they can coexist; side by side in space becomes side by side in time.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西在同一段上并行、谁也不挤走谁，就可以共存；空间上的并排因此转成时间上的「并存」。

intro.en: Alongside is a transparent English compound of along and side, and it began as a sailor's word.
intro.cn: alongside 是 along 与 side 组成的透明复合词，最初是水手的用语。

items.en: The first element is andlang, the whole length of, built from and- plus lang long.
items.cn: 第一部分是 andlang「整条长度」，由 and- 加 lang「长」构成。

items.en: Side meant flank or the long edge of a thing, and it is the second element of the compound.
items.cn: side 意为「侧面、长边」，是这个复合词的第二部分。

items.en: The compound is recorded in nautical writing in the eighteenth century, meaning close to the side of a ship; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词一般认为自十八世纪起见于航海文字，意为「贴近船舷」；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The meaning widened from ships to anything with a side, such as roads, rivers and buildings.
items.cn: 词义从船只扩展到一切有侧边的东西，如道路、河流与建筑。

items.en: The figurative sense together with, and the fuller American form alongside of, become common in ordinary prose.
items.cn: 引申义「与……一起」以及美式完整形式 alongside of 在普通书面语中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the two elements of the compound, the shore compound built on the same first element, and the old form in -st; the near-meaning group holds words for side, equality and addition.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词的两个成分、用同一前项构成的沿岸词，以及带 -st 的旧形式；近义组收表示侧旁、并列与附加的词。

entries.definition: The first element of the compound, meaning from one end towards the other.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的第一部分，义为「沿着、从一端到另一端」。

entries.definition: The second element, meaning the flank or long edge of something.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的第二部分，义为某物的侧面或长边。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning along the shore, built on the same along- element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与副词，义为「沿岸的、沿着海岸」，由同一个 along- 成分构成。

entries.definition: An old form meaning along, now found only in older texts.
entries.definitionCN: 旧形式，义同 along「沿着」，今只见于较早的文本。

entries.definition: At the side of something; like alongside, but without the idea of running the whole length.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」；与 alongside 相近，但不含「沿着整段」的意思。

entries.definition: Side by side and facing the same way; the closest match for the parallel sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「并排地、并肩地」，与 alongside 的「并排」义最接近。

entries.definition: In addition to; it looks like beside but has moved into the sense of addition, as along with can.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「除……之外、此外」；形似 beside，却和 along with 一样转向了「附加」义。

entries.definition: Running in the same direction at a constant distance; the geometric picture behind side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与名词，义为「平行的、平行线」，正是「并排」背后的几何画面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two visible elements along and side, the nautical origin, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用看得见的两个成分 along 与 side、它的航海来源，以及这个词常出现的短语。

normal.en: Along plus side: a whole length laid against a side.
normal.cn: along 加 side：把一整条长度贴到一个侧边上。

normal.en: The word began with boats, because a ship's side is the most literal side there is.
normal.cn: 这个词从船开始，因为船舷是最字面意义上的「侧边」。

normal.en: Work alongside keeps the same picture, with people standing where boats once stood.
normal.cn: work alongside 保留同一个画面，只是把船换成了人。

normal.en: Alongside of only adds of, so the side relation is spelled out.
normal.cn: alongside of 只是多加一个 of，把「在旁边」的关系说白。

normal.en: Two old customs surviving alongside each other are simply two things on one line.
normal.cn: 两种并存的老习俗，不过是同一条线上的两样东西。

abstract.en: Two hulls float so close that the paint on both sides almost touches.
abstract.cn: 两条船身贴得极近，两侧的漆几乎碰到一起。

abstract.en: Two runners keep the same stride on two parallel tracks for the whole race.
abstract.cn: 两名跑者在两条平行跑道上，整场保持同样的步幅。

abstract.en: Take the boat away and the two sides remain, still parallel, still level.
abstract.cn: 把船移走，两条边还在，仍然平行，仍然齐平。

examples.en: A row of poplars grows alongside the railway.
examples.cn: 一排白杨沿着铁路生长。

examples.en: Nurses worked alongside the doctors through the whole night.
examples.cn: 护士们整夜与医生并肩工作。

examples.en: Old fishing customs survive alongside modern tourism in the village.
examples.cn: 在这个村子里，古老的捕鱼习俗与现代旅游业并存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿朗赛德」——两条船把船舷贴在一起：在……旁边；与……一起。

root: 由 along 与 side 复合而成：along 来自古英语 andlang「整条长度」，side 意为「侧面、长边」。十八世纪起在航海文字中表示「贴近船舷」，十九世纪扩展到道路、河流、建筑等一切有侧边之物，再由「并排」引申出「与……一起」「并存」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses keep one geometry: a length laid against a side. The side can belong to a road, a partner, a pier, or another custom that simply coexists.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项保持同一个几何关系：把一条长度贴到一个侧边上。这个侧边可以属于道路、伙伴、码头，也可以属于另一种只是并存着的习俗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges run parallel, so close that they almost touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边并行延伸，近得几乎相触。

branches.en: THE SIDE: one length is laid beside another, and the two run parallel.
branches.cn: 侧边线：一条长度被贴到另一条旁边，两者并行。

branches.en: THE COMPANY: standing side by side becomes working together, and then merely existing at the same time.
branches.cn: 共处线：并排而立变成一起工作，再退一步就是同时存在。

branches.en: THE HARBOUR: the compound's oldest home is a boat lying against a ship or a pier.
branches.cn: 港湾线：这个复合词最早的家，是一条船贴住另一条船或码头。

branches.en: THE ADVERB: with the object left out, the word simply says that something is close to the side.
branches.cn: 副词线：省略宾语后，这个词只说明某物贴近侧边。

branches.en: THE FULLER FORM: of is added to make the side relation explicit.
branches.cn: 完整形式线：加上 of，把侧边关系说白。

intro.en: Alongside is built from the compound along plus side, and the same first element recurs in alongshore.
intro.cn: alongside 由复合词 along 加 side 构成，同一个前项又出现在 alongshore 里。

latinIntro.en: Every element here is Germanic, so there is no Latin cognate and the Latin column stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的每个成分都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语同源词，所以拉丁语一栏留空。
